1Where is Ummo, and which star does it orbit?According to the letters, Ummo follows an elliptical orbit around the star IUMMA, which terrestrial astronomers call Wolf 424 D41-1 p.79 D41-1 p.80. It would be seen from Earth in the constellation of Virgo D21 p.6. The first letter gives an “apparent” distance of 14.437 light-years and a “real” distance of 3.685 light-years, measured in a ten-dimensional space D21 p.5. The planet’s radius would be 7,251.63 km, about 14% more than that of Earth, and its gravity 11.88 m/s² D41-1 p.80.Link to this question2How long is a day, a year, and how do they measure time?The Ummite day, the XII, lasts 600 UIW, or 30.92 Earth hours D41-3 p.91; noon falls at 300 UIW, and 25 UIW make a little over one Earth hour D41-3 p.92. One UIW is worth about 3.1 minutes D41-2 p.89. The year, the XEE, has 60 Ummite days and is worth 0.2118 of an Earth year, or about two and a half months D41-2 p.85 D43 p.180. The planet is divided into 25 time zones whose origin is a small equatorial island, like Greenwich NR-18 p.1392. The letters warn that Ummite and Earth dates cannot be exactly synchronised D57-1 p.255.Link to this question3What are Ummo’s continent, seas and climate like?The oceans cover about 62% of the surface; the rest forms a single continent full of large lakes, with a few islands D41-1 p.80 D84 p.562. The relief is heavily eroded; the largest lake covers 276,320 km² D41-1 p.80. “Volcanoes” in the form of crevasses throw up incandescent columns of methane and oxygen that light up the nights D41-1 p.80 D41-6 p.113. Half of the continent is a nature reserve, and the polar zone is icy and deserted NR-18 p.1391 NR-18 p.1392. The nights are cold and intensely dark D41-3 p.92 D41-9 p.130; in the morning, the temperature may be around 3 °C D41-3 p.93.Link to this question4Which plants and animals live on Ummo?According to the letters, flora and fauna are less varied than on Earth, but the vegetation is exuberant D41-2 p.86. The typical trees are the NAANAA, the IGUU, close to the ancient tree ferns, and the OAXAUXAA D41-5 p.100 D41-6 p.113. There would be no true birds, but many flying mammals, such as the OIXIIXI, whose milk is used in cooking D41-5 p.107. People eat the meat of the OOGIXUAA, a vertebrate close to the reptiles D41-5 p.107, the AIMMOA fruit, a staple food D41-5 p.106, and the INOWII, a juicy fruit D41-4 p.97. New species of large-flowered plants have been created in the laboratory D41-6 p.113.Link to this question5Does the map attached to D41-1 show the whole planet?No, according to the late letters. NR-18 explains that the map of D41-1 D41-1 p.81 represents only the region of the WOAROO AAXAA peninsula, around the seat NR-18 p.1390 NR-18 p.1391; NR-22 gives its dimensions, about 420 × 276 KOAEE NR-22 p.1411. The site’s globe therefore does not use this map for the whole surface. The reconstruction of the region, with its lakes, is still being verified.Link to this question6Does Ummo have a moon?The letters mention none. D41-3 writes that the nights are “intensely dark” and that the Ummites cannot enjoy, as Earthlings do, the spectacle of the “lunar satellite” D41-3 p.92 D41-3 p.93. The most visible body in their sky is NAWEE, a gas giant that orbits their star closer in than Ummo: it is not a moon NR-21 p.1407 NR-21 p.1408.Link to this question

7What do the Ummites look like physically?The letters describe a body whose morphology is “analogous” to that of terrestrial Homo sapiens, with only small differences D21 p.8 D41-1 p.81. Sexual morphology differs very little from ours D41-13 p.145. A small transducer is placed on the larynx from childhood D33-3 p.59 D99 p.595. One letter mentions a chemical compound in the hair and a yellowish pigmentation on an unspecified area of the body D99 p.595. A letter from 2013 warns that some may surprise “by their stature or particular physical features” GR1-9 p.1458. On Earth, they say they mingle with people by passing themselves off as foreigners D33-3 p.61.Link to this question8Why can most Ummites not speak?According to the letters, a large part of the inhabitants of Ummo “lack a voice” D41-2 p.88. At around 14 to 16 years of age, the vocal cords become sclerotic and the person falls silent; they then develop telepathic communication D41-1 p.82. A small transducer the size of a lens, placed on the larynx at the age of two, amplifies the faint remaining voice D33-3 p.59 D99 p.595. The expeditionaries on Earth say they belong to a minority that can still speak, with the help of miniaturised equipment in the throat D41-2 p.88.Link to this question9How do they communicate with one another (bi-language, telepathy)?As children, the Ummites speak a “bi-language”: by repeating each phoneme a certain number of times, they express two streams of ideas at once, for example “OA DO DO IA KAAWAEA UMMO UMMO UMMO” D41-1 p.82. As adults, they communicate by telepathy, in impulses of 0.00014 second D41-1 p.82. At home, ultrasonic whistles control the furniture that rises from the floor D41-2 p.88 D41-4 p.96. A letter from 2003 states that the telepathic link would be the only one to allow simultaneous contact between two star systems NR-18 p.1392.Link to this question10How long do they live, and how are their children born and raised?According to a letter from 2003, death is, barring accidents, a voluntary act between 91 and 121 Earth years; otherwise, longevity could exceed 140 years NR-18 p.1393. Procreation takes place only within the couple: the first child is a right and a duty, the second requires authorisation NR-18 p.1392 NR-18 p.1393. The child trains every day in the audiovisual room of the home and reaches learning autonomy at around 8 years NR-18 p.1393. During training at the UNAWO WI, the child hardly sees their parents D41-2 p.85. At around 8 years, children already take part in household tasks D41-4 p.96.Link to this question11How does education work on Ummo?According to the letters, with equal aptitudes, everyone receives the same training, in the teaching colony of the UNAWO WI; it lasts from 9.46 XEE (about two years) to 28 XEE (a little under six years), depending on a psychotechnical assessment D41-6 p.109. Thanks to the bi-language, a teacher can set out two disciplines in a single utterance D41-1 p.82. During this training, young people must neither see nor hear their parents, except on rare occasions D41-2 p.85. One letter recounts that an attempt to remodel brains was abandoned in favour of educating natural abilities D47-4 p.221 D47-4 p.222.Link to this question

12How is Ummo governed?The letters describe three levels. All citizens in full possession of their faculties make the laws: each group of 12 chooses a representative, and 1,728 representatives elect a delegate who proposes and votes on the laws D68-1 p.425. A council of at most 116 members judges and watches over the balance of powers; at the summit, the UMMOAELEWEE has four members, chosen as children for their exceptional faculties D68-1 p.427. Leaders are subject to the laws like everyone else, and the computer network informs each person of their rights D68-1 p.426. In 1966, 28 of the 116 members of the sub-council were women D41-13 p.149.Link to this question13Who was IE 456, and what is the period of tyranny?According to letters D41-15 and D43, I4IE 456 is a precocious woman scientist elected supreme leader; on the 17th day of her rule, she has nine of her twelve advisers executed and governs alone D41-15 p.154. She makes scientific research the supreme goal, in a climate of terror in which vivisections are cited D41-15 p.155. At her death, her daughter W1WIE 1, aged 12, succeeds her without being elected D43 p.182. The regime is said to have caused at least four million victims; it ends with an explosive, followed by a period of hatred of science D41-15 p.156. It is in this context that UUMMOWOA appears D43 p.181.Link to this question14Who was UMMOWOA, and what is his message?The letters describe UUMMOWOA as the “divine man” of Ummo, born under the former leader OES 17 D43 p.180. A forced labourer at a large solar power plant, he spreads his teachings in secret D43 p.181 D43 p.182. On night 15 of the year 1402, he gives himself up to the police so as not to compromise his followers, then undergoes martyrdom; his body disappears at the moment of his death D43 p.184. He leaves about 1,200 aphorisms, the TAAU D43 p.182, including: “Never say WOA WAS or WOA WILL BE, always say WOA IS” D43 p.185. His central principle: to respect and love other human beings D43 p.186. D43 compares his figure to that of Jesus D43 p.185.Link to this question15How does the economy work, without money or trade?According to the letters, money does not exist as it does on Earth: each person accumulates remuneration according to their abilities and output, held by the computer network D41-13 p.148. No one owns capital goods (machines, vehicles, buildings) as private property D41-16 p.177. The synthetic production of food is said to be so abundant that there is no longer any problem of distribution D41-16 p.177. Products arrive in every home through underground tubes: nothing is “bought” D41-4 p.97 D41-4 p.98. The working day lasts only 50 to 75 UIW, or 2.58 to 3.87 hours D41-3 p.92. One letter describes this society as socialist and deeply religious D41-16 p.179.Link to this question16What place do women and couples have?According to the letters, within the home the wife submits to her husband’s authority without losing her right to an opinion, but before the State she has the same rights as the man D41-13 p.149. Engagements include a purely tactile phase, and the interval between puberty and marriage must remain short D41-13 p.147. After marriage, the couple chooses its home by consulting the computer network D41-13 p.148. Procreation is reserved to the couple, the OMGEEYIE NR-18 p.1392. In the day described, household tasks rotate between husband and wife D41-4 p.96. Women are said to be better than men in the art of perfumes D41-3 p.94.Link to this question17How are serious offences punished?According to D33-3, the death penalty does not exist on Ummo: every offender becomes “property of the People”, and the penalty follows a legal code common to the whole planet D33-3 p.49. The letter mentions daily spiritual and technical re-education and a “humiliating penalty of nudity” that can be lifted D33-3 p.49. A letter from 1987 states that the damage done is assessed rather than the intention, and that the penalty is an educational response D791 p.855.Link to this question

18What does an Ummite house look like?The house, the XAABI, is mushroom-shaped: a tower carries an inhabited dome D41-2 p.86. A piston driven by sodium vapour makes it rise, “almost always at nightfall”, or descend to ground level D41-2 p.88. It has five or six rooms with no fixed function D41-2 p.88. The floor bears coloured shapes that are hatches from which the furniture emerges; the orange rectangle corresponds to the seat D41-2 p.89. The roof is made of transparent panels, removed every other night to sleep under the open sky, and no window looks onto the outside D41-3 p.92.Link to this question19What does a typical day look like?The letters follow a family from waking to bedtime. At 196 UIW, they wake without an alarm clock D41-3 p.93; the father gathers the family and gives the instructions for the day D41-3 p.94, then comes a scented steam bath D41-3 p.95. At 225 UIW the first meal takes place, the most copious D41-5 p.100. At 246 UIW, the husband leaves for work D41-6 p.109, for only 50 to 75 UIW D41-3 p.92. At around 575 UIW, the couple withdraw for meditation, then sleep D41-9 p.130 D41-9 p.131. The illustrated account “A day on Ummo” follows these stages one by one.Link to this question20What do they eat, and how?Food arrives at the house through underground tubes, in standardised cylinders D41-4 p.97 D41-4 p.98, and an automatic kitchen programmed by titanium memory prepares the dishes D41-4 p.99. The first meal, at dawn, is the most copious D41-5 p.100. It begins with a few UIW of silence D41-5 p.103; broths are sipped through long tubes, without a spoon D41-5 p.104. For solid foods, eaten with the fingers, a thin film protects the hands D41-5 p.104 D41-5 p.105, and an ultraviolet-beam “cutter” replaces the knife D41-5 p.105. On the menu: the AIMMOA, a staple food D41-5 p.106, and OOGIXUAA meat D41-5 p.107.Link to this question21How do they dress?According to the letters, clothes are made at home a few UIW before being worn, then thrown away and disintegrated: “We do not know fabrics” D41-5 p.100. On waking, people cover themselves with a round cape pierced for the head and arms, the GIUDUUDAA EEWE D41-3 p.93. For work, the husband wears a close-fitting suit whose colours (here yellow circles on a purple background) form a code of trades D41-6 p.109. In the ships, each traveller wears a membrane that surrounds the body without touching the skin D69-1 p.445. On Earth, the expeditionaries wear local clothing D37-2 p.70.Link to this question22How do they get around on their planet?The most widely used vehicle is the GOONIIOADOO UEWA, which flies 0.56 m above the ground, piloted by the computer network; the probability of an accident is said to be 0.00007 D41-6 p.110 D41-6 p.111. For short distances, body-fitted equipment, the OEMMIIUEWA, allows flight up to 56 m high D41-6 p.110. The old NOIA UEWA walked on articulated feet D41-6 p.111. Roads have been removed so as not to spoil the landscape, and goods circulate underground D41-6 p.112.Link to this question23Do the Ummites have music?The letters do not say the same thing. NR-21 (2009) describes music made of crystalline sounds and xylophone-like percussion, and judges terrestrial music more accomplished than any they know NR-21 p.1403. GR1-3 (2012) states on the contrary that the Ummites have never cultivated art and cannot compose music, even though they appreciate it GR1-3 p.1428 GR1-3 p.1429.Link to this question

24Who is WOA?WOA is the Generator, what Earthlings call God D33-1 p.41. According to the letters, he introduced an “intelligent” asymmetry into the cosmos: the Creation D731 p.830. The mathematicians of Ummo call the sinusoidal function the “mathematical generator of the Generator or God” D45 p.197. An aphorism of UUMMOWOA says: “always say WOA IS” D43 p.185. The Ummites say they do not beg WOA, but convey their gratitude to him D79 p.544.Link to this question25What is the BUUAWAA, the soul?The letters describe a human being made of three factors: the body, the OEMII; the soul, the BUUAWAA; and a third factor that links them, krypton atoms in the brain D84 p.563 D33-2 p.46. A letter from 1966 recounts the discovery of these atoms by an Ummite researcher D33-3 p.47 D33-3 p.48. Death corresponds to the disappearance of these atoms D357-2 p.738. The moment when the soul unites with the body varies between letters: “a few hours after” fertilisation in 1987 D539 p.801, “at the precise instant” of fertilisation in 2013 GR1-10 p.1465. The spelling of the word varies as well D105-1 p.631.Link to this question26What is the BUUAWE BIAEII, the collective spirit?The BUUAWE BIAEII, abbreviated BB, designates the collective soul of a humanity, and the universe that contains all the collective souls D33-3 p.53 D357-2 p.740. According to the letters of 1987, a network of krypton atoms links each organism to this universe, where information is encoded; the letter compares it to the “collective unconscious” D731 p.822. Each BB cell corresponds to the set of living beings of one planet D731 p.828 D731 p.829. In return, BB would guide the evolution of living beings and transmit universal ideas to humans D731 p.831.Link to this question27What happens after death?According to a letter from 1987, at death, the krypton atoms cease their function and the soul connects to BB D357-2 p.738. If the life violated moral laws, the soul’s information is first “reconformed” at a low rate: what Earthlings call purgatory, a “distortion of the informative flow” that is not eternal D357-2 p.738 D791 p.854. Afterwards, the soul shares the knowledge of humanity and communicates with the souls of the deceased D357-2 p.738 D357-2 p.739. The letters of 2013 say that reincarnation “does not exist”, apart from some thirty unexplained cases GR1-8 p.1451 GR1-8 p.1452. On Ummo, the body is converted into helium during a family ceremony NR-18 p.1393 NR-18 p.1394.Link to this question28What do the letters say about Jesus and terrestrial religions?Letter D43 compares UUMMOWOA to Jesus, called OYAGAAWOA D43 p.185. According to D792 (1988), Jesus, crucified, does not die; he resumes his preaching and then disappears before 1,200 to 1,500 witnesses, and the Shroud of Turin did indeed wrap his body D792-2 p.890 D792-2 p.894. The letters of 1988 also assert that the dating of the shroud was carried out on a substituted sample D488 p.773. In a conversation of 1987, an Ummite says that Jesus and UUMMOWOA are two distinct envoys H2 p.1272. A letter of 1988 states that there is no institutionalised religion on Ummo D792-1 p.860 D792-1 p.862.Link to this question

29What are the WAAM and the WAAM-WAAM, the multiple universes?The WAAM is a universe; the WAAM-WAAM is the set of universes, the pluricosmos D33-1 p.43. According to the letters, the real universe is made up of pairs of cosmos, each dominated by one type of mass, positive or negative; the authors suspect an infinity of pairs D731 p.816. Our twin cosmos, the UWAAM D33-1 p.43, folds ours, which makes it possible to travel faster than light D45 p.193 D731 p.816. At the “beginning”, the WAAM contained all its mass in an unstable nucleus that exploded, and WOA introduced an “intelligent” asymmetry into it D731 p.830.Link to this question30How do they travel between the stars?According to the letters, space folds under the influence of the twin cosmos, like a sheet that a gust of wind draws towards itself D45 p.193. Travel is possible only when these folds bring two stars closer together, which can be predicted only in the short term D57-1 p.260. The ship then “inverts” all its particles to pass into another three-dimensional frame: this is the OAWOOLEAIDAA D57-1 p.259 D69-2 p.452. To an observer, the inverted matter seems to disappear D69-2 p.453. In 1950, three ships were thus said to have “appeared” above Digne D57-3 p.271.Link to this question31What is the IBOZOO UU?The IBOZOO UU is, according to the letters, the elementary entity of which everything is made: a bundle of orthogonal axes, linked to others by relations of angles D59-2 p.326. It occupies no defined position and does not exist in time: it is itself time D59-2 p.319 D59-2 p.320. Particles would be merely different orientations of one and the same IBOZOO UU D59-2 p.326. When a proton becomes energy, its axis would have rotated by 90°: “a change of axis, that is, a change of dimension” D57-1 p.259. A living being would be a network of IBOZOO UU whose internal entropy decreases D731 p.832.Link to this question32What is their mathematics (base 12)?The first letter explains that the Ummites count in base 12, although they have ten fingers like us, for “purely historical” reasons D21 p.6. Their images are stored in a titanium crystal in a “duodecimal” system, not a binary one D41-11 p.139, and their XANMOO computer also works in base 12 D71 p.504. Letter D45 details their signs for the sum, equality, the integral or the hyperbolic sine D45 p.196 D45 p.197. They use two logics, one with two values like ours, the other with four D68-1 p.424. The Writing chapter presents their numerals.Link to this question33What do they say about other inhabited planets?According to D41-16, Ummo has visited 218 planets without life or with primary life; first contact with a civilisation took place with the planet IEYIOBAA, and the second ended with the death of all six crew members D41-16 p.176. The letters also speak of messages from very far away, one of them from the Andromeda galaxy D41-16 p.175. D41-1 mentions the arrival of ships from another planet in year 75 of their 3rd era D41-1 p.81 D541 p.813. An Ummite says, in 1987, that they take great care not to interfere in the evolution of other planets H2 p.1271. A tweet from 2020 relays a map of seven inhabited worlds within 30 light-years W5 p.1711.Link to this question

43What do they think of humanity?Their view is mixed. They say they were “surprised and moved” by the sensitivity of their correspondents D50 p.231, and acknowledge that Earthlings are superior in music D41-3 p.94; the arts are said to be poorer on Ummo D41-16 p.179. But they criticise large cities, “monsters of concrete, asphalt and steel” D41-3 p.93, or the game of chess, judged sterile D41-8 p.129. Their civilisation is said to be more advanced because humanity there is much older D58-2 p.287. In the day described, they are surprised that Earth medicine ignores the role of calm in digestion D41-5 p.103.Link to this question44What do they say about nuclear war and the dangers to come?In autumn 1973, letters mention a threat of nuclear war and offer refuges to a few friends D113 p.664; D170-1 announces that all the Ummites will leave Earth at the end of 1973 D170-1 p.693. In 1979, a letter describes research on plasma weapons D117 p.677 D117 p.678. In 1980 and 1983, the letters explain that Ummo cannot intervene directly D118 p.681 D119 p.686 D176 p.706. In 1988, a letter is entitled “Intervention plan to save the Earth” D1378 p.908. In one conversation, an Ummite speaks of the risk of nuclear war H6 p.1296.Link to this question45What do they say about UFOs and other visitors?As early as 1966, the letters say that sightings of craft that do not come from Ummo are, setting aside illusions and hoaxes, “of the galactic type”; the Ummites cannot identify them D21 p.11. 46Who received the letters, and from when?According to the letters, before 1966 contacts were limited to scientists D21 p.5; in 1961, an astrophysicist at the Fabra Observatory is said to have received data D21 p.10. The first contact with Fernando FSSesma dates from 14 January 1966, and a Madrid typist types the letters from February onwards D21 p.10 D21 p.11. The first letter is distributed in 28 copies D21 p.3. Next come Dionisio DGGarrido, Enrique EVVillagrasa, RFRafael Farriols, ARAntonio Ribera, Juan JAAguirre and JBJorge Barrenechea D59-1 p.310 D62-4 p.368 D72 p.510 D112 p.657 D357-1 p.716 D539 p.797. In 1992, the Frenchman JPJean-Pierre Petit receives a letter NR-5 p.1361, and in 2003 an anonymous recipient nicknamed “PMPierre Martain” NR-13 p.1375. The Key figures page presents their links.Link to this question47What happened at Aluche and San José de Valderas?According to the letters, on 6 February 1966 at 20:02, a ship lands near Aluche, in the suburbs of Madrid D37-2 p.70; witnesses see it D37-1 p.68 and capsules are picked up D38 p.73. On 1 June 1967 at 20:20, a ship is observed and photographed at San José de Valderas; its arrival had been announced by letter D60 p.350. The photos are published under the name of Antonio Pardo E19 p.1010. In 2005, JLJosé Luis Jordán Peña states that these photos are his E41 p.1210.Link to this question48Who is José Luis Jordán Peña and what did he state?Born in Alicante in 1931 E45 p.1237, JLJordán Peña was one of the first correspondents: as early as 1966, he gave testimony about Aluche E18 p.1007, and the letters often cite him D73 p.517 D470 p.772. In April 1993, in letters to RFRafael Farriols, he writes that he wrote “almost all” of the Ummo reports, until illness prevented him, and that the later writings were forged E49 p.1248 E51 p.1254. In 2005, he states that he is the author of the San José de Valderas photos E41 p.1210. The editors of the compilation note that many do not believe him E41 p.1208. He died in 2014; his death notice bears the symbol )+( E45 p.1235 E45 p.1236.Link to this question49How many letters are there, and how are they classified?This site contains 292 documents drawn from the Ummo-Sciences compilation (21 April 2025). They are divided into series: D for letters, E for external documents, H for conversations, NR and GR1 for late letters, W for social networks. The classification follows that of RFRafael Farriols’s volumes D21 p.3 and Ignacio IDDarnaude’s catalogue D41-16 p.175. The editors sometimes vote on the classification of a document: this is the case for the letter on the Gulf War D1751 p.937.Link to this question50Why do the letters bear a purple stamp?The editors note that the stamp is “usually” purple, and point out as an exception a letter with a green stamp D26 p.20 D54 p.248. The compilation gives no reason for this colour. A typist reports that the Ummites affixed their seal themselves with a kind of ring worn on the finger E29 p.1049. A 1979 letter invites the reader to verify its authenticity by means of the seal D116 p.672, and another asks to receive anyone who presents themselves with a code “validated by our stamp” D113 p.667. In 1993, JLJordán Peña asserts that the seal was “perfectly forged” E51 p.1254.Link to this question51What are the “late letters” and the tweets?After 1993, letters become rare. In 2003, three letters in French signed EIE IXOO 7 reach an anonymous recipient NR-13 p.1375 NR-15 p.1382 NR-18 p.1390. From 2011 to 2014, the GR1 series gives instructions for meetings GR1-1 p.1422 GR1-9 p.1457 GR1-11 p.1466. Finally, the compilation contains messages published on Twitter from 2012 to 2024 W1 p.1469 W4 p.1702 W5 p.1706. The edition classifies them separately: this site flags them as “tweets” so that they are not confused with the letters.Link to this question52Do the letters make verifiable predictions?The compilation contains no systematic assessment of the predictions. It does contain a few dated announcements: one letter announces the arrival of a ship for 1 June 1967, and the San José de Valderas observation takes place that day D60 p.350, but JLJordán Peña would later claim the photos E41 p.1210. A 1973 letter announces the departure of all the Ummites with a probability of return of 65.14% D170-1 p.693. Other passages propose technical ideas, such as a sound recorder with no moving parts D66 p.410. This site reports these assertions without judging them.Link to this question53How should this file be read with caution?The file itself points out apocryphal letters attributed to the Ummites D116 p.672 and reports “fraudulently attributed to Ummo” D392 p.755. Some documents are edited as being of non-Ummite origin, for example the typists’ letters E26 p.1042. Ummo dates cannot be exactly synchronised with those of Earth D57-1 p.255. JLJordán Peña claimed to be the author of most of the letters E49 p.1248. The Ummite calendar is counted back from a single landmark: letter D541, written in 1987, says that it is then year 5,923 of the 3rd era D541 p.812. Each era lasts 6,000 Ummo years, roughly 1,270 Earth years D541 p.812. But between the end of the 2nd era and the start of the 3rd, the letter places a period of 11,750 Ummo years, roughly 2,488 Earth years, the “dark night of Ummo” (AGFUIUU DUUA): it “lasted”, but it is “not taken into account” in their numbering of years D541 p.813.Placed on our calendar, it would run from about 1,755 BC to about AD 730. It therefore changes nothing in the dates of the 3rd era, counted directly from 1987. By contrast, everything that precedes it, the 1st and 2nd eras, moves back by about 2,488 years when it is counted. Yet the six inventions compared here all date from the 1st or 2nd era, before the dark night.Current display: dark night counted. This is the reading most faithful to D541, since the period really did last: the Ummite inventions compared then range from about 4,060 to 1,865 BC, and the lead over Earth is about 4,900 years. The Earth dates are conversions made by this site; the letters give only the era and the year. In the letters’ account, each invention of Ummo has a later Earth equivalent. D541 says that the divine figure of Jesus of Galilee would have emerged on Earth around year 2,541 of the 2nd era of Ummo D541 p.812. This landmark only works with the idealised scheme: counting the dark night, year 2,541 of the 2nd era corresponds to about −2,490, whereas Jesus is born in the middle of the dark night, a period that the Ummites do not number. Interpretation proposed by this site, which the letters do not state: lacking an Ummo year for this period, the letter would have counted back from the start of the 3rd era, around 732, without the dark night, which gives year 2,541 of the 2nd era. This would be the origin of the discrepancy between the two readings. UUMMOWOA, the “divine man” of Ummo, is born in year 1,282 of the 2nd era D541 p.812, that is around −2,757 when the dark night is counted. How this estimate is calculated, and its limits For each invention, letter D541 gives the Ummo year in which it appears D541 p.812. I convert it into an Earth year from the letter’s landmark: 4.72 Ummo years equal one Earth year D57-1 p.256 and 1987 corresponds to year 5,923 of the 3rd era D541 p.812. By default, the “dark night”, which lasted 11,750 Ummo years, or about 2,488 Earth years D541 p.813, is counted. The letter’s idealised scheme ignores it and places Jesus around year 2,541 of the 2nd era D541 p.812: the inventions of the first two eras then appear about 2,488 years more recent, and the lead falls to about 2,400 years (button above). The letters give no estimate of this gap: it is a calculation made here. The choice of the Earth equivalent is mine: only photography is a direct match, one other is proposed by the letter itself (printing), and the rest are close or approximate. The estimate assumes that the letters’ account is accurate, without judging it. The letter itself specifies that the synchronisation is idealised D541 p.812: the order of magnitude is therefore more reliable than the figures.

II · Ummo according to the letters › Knowledge›Chapter 23 of 31Knowledge · Chapter 23The XANMOO, Ummo’s Computers The letters describe computers that are both digital and analogue, which calculate in base 12 and keep their data in the quantum state of titanium atoms. This chapter gathers what the letters say about them, then compares the titanium memory with today’s computers and quantum memories.

The idea in one sentence. In 1967, letter D71 compares, point by point, the Earth computing of the time (valves, transistors, ferrite cores, punched cards) with that of Ummo. The XANMMO BAA is “simultaneously digital and analogue”: for a geometry problem, it gives the area of a hyperbola of revolution in figures, its graph and its three-dimensional visualisation. D71 p.504Where Earth computers encode in binary, Ummo’s calculation circuits and memories operate in base 12. D71 p.504 D71 p.505The ODU GOAA replaces the valve and the transistor: a neutron causes the fission of a single atom, whose heat is then converted into electricity. The letter insists: unlike our amplifiers, its efficiency exceeds unity. D71 p.505 D71 p.506The IYOAEE BOO calculation circuits use a few hundred “chemo-nuclear” reactions on controlled micromasses, in place of transistors. D71 p.506The XANWAABUASII DIIO memory replaces older photoelectric selenium memories, which had become too bulky. DAOO 6, son of DAOO 4, had the idea of encoding the digits on an IBOAAYANOA base, which the letter translates as “quantum”. Ummo never used magnetic memory. The idea in one sentence. The XANMOO are not reserved for scientists: a planetary network, household appliances and the ships all depend on them. There are 120 giant XANMOO AYUBAA on Ummo, linked to a large central memory located on the island of GOABAAAE; they “regulate all the activity” of the planet. D41-16 p.177 D41-16 p.178This central unit stores everyone’s remuneration in mathematical form: money does not exist as it does on Earth. D41-13 p.148Anyone who doubts their rights queries the network, which answers “phonetically and graphically”. D68-1 p.426Vehicles speed along 0.56 m above the ground, following the terrain; the probability of an accident is reduced to 0.00007. D41-6 p.111At home, the UAMIIXANMOO is an automatic kitchen “programmed by titanium memory”. D41-4 p.96In the ships, the XANMOO are not electronic: they are made of organs integrated into stable crystals, the ODU GOOA. A XANMOO receives the data of each traveller’s body through about 2.16 million channels. D69-1 p.448 D69-1 p.445In 1969, letter D83 gives the density of titanium memories: from 8·10¹⁷ to 5.3·10²⁰ bits per cm³, in base 12, on “the quantum states” of the components of a crystal. D83 p.549 A consistency check. One cm³ of titanium contains about 5.7·10²² atoms. At ten states per atom (3.3 bits), the theoretical maximum is about 1.9·10²³ bits per cm³. The density given in D83 (5.3·10²⁰) is about 1/355th of that: this corresponds to a digit written a few hundred times, which is what D71 announced two years earlier (“hundreds and thousands of times”). The two letters are consistent with each other.

The idea in one sentence. Each digit is written in the energy level of the electrons of a titanium atom, which three crossed beams come to target one at a time. The block must be a perfect crystal, of 100% purity: a few atoms of iron, molybdenum or silicon make it unusable. D71 p.507Three orthogonal beams, with a frequency close to 8.35·10²¹ Hz, pass through the block without effect. Where they cross, their “beat” (heterodyne) gives a much lower frequency, which falls on a titanium line: only that atom is excited. D71 p.507 D71 p.508Each atom uses ten states, linked to ten spectral lines; a base-12 digit therefore requires two atoms. D71 p.508Reading returns the atom to its initial state: each digit is written hundreds or thousands of times. D71 p.508The crystal works “at a temperature practically equal to absolute zero”, otherwise thermal agitation would make it impossible to locate the atoms. D71 p.508

The idea in one sentence. D71 requires a crystal “at a temperature practically equal to absolute zero” to immobilise the atoms D71 p.508; our quantum computers, too, have had to go down close to absolute zero, for two reasons that must be told apart. Current platformWhat is cooledTemperatureWhy Superconducting circuits (Google, IBM)The whole chip, in a dilution refrigerator≈ 0.01 KTo prevent heat from exciting the qubit and to remove electrical resistance. Spins in siliconThe chip≈ 0.1 to 1 KTo avoid thermal excitation and noise from neighbouring electrons. Trapped ionsThe motion of the ions, by laser (the enclosure is often at room temperature)motion close to the ground stateTo keep each ion still and addressable, and to make two-ion gates work. Neutral atoms in optical tweezersThe motion of the atoms, by lasera few µKTo keep each atom in place and targeted by its beam. Rare-earth memoriesThe host crystal≈ 2 to 4 KTo reduce the lattice vibrations that blur the levels. Diamond NV centres, photonsNothing, or only the detectorsroom temperature possibleTheir levels withstand heat. First reason: thermal excitation. A superconducting qubit at 5 GHz has an energy corresponding to about 0.24 K: the temperature must be brought well below that for it to stay in its ground state. This is the main reason at Google and IBM. It does not apply to the D71 lines: for a line at 335 nm, the equivalent temperature is about 43,000 K. Second reason: the motion of atoms. This is the reason in D71, and it is the same as for trapped ions and neutral atoms: a vibrating atom moves out of the beam aiming at it. Laser cooling, which makes this possible, was not achieved until 1978. On this specific point, the letter anticipates a real practice. A physical limit. Even at absolute zero, an atom is never motionless: quantum mechanics leaves it a “zero-point motion”. In titanium, the average vibration amplitude goes from about 0.13 Å at 300 K to about 0.07 Å at absolute zero. Cold reduces the agitation by roughly half, without eliminating it. Temperature: 300 K 50 %chance that a 5 GHz superconducting qubit is excited by heat< 10⁻¹²chance that a titanium atom is excited on the 335 nm line0.128 Åaverage vibration amplitude of an atom in the titanium crystal Calculations by the site: Boltzmann factor for the first two boxes; Debye model of titanium (Debye temperature ≈ 420 K), as an order of magnitude, for the third. Two neighbouring atoms are about 2.9 Å apart. What already existed in 1967. Liquid helium (4.2 K) had been obtained since 1908; the first dilution refrigerator, which reaches the millikelvin range, was operating in Leiden in 1964; since the cryotron of 1956, laboratories (including IBM) had been studying superconducting computer memories immersed in liquid helium. The idea of a computer cooled close to absolute zero was therefore not unknown. What D71 adds is the link between this cold and the addressing of individual atoms.
The idea in one sentence. Several technical details of D71 can be checked by calculation; some do not correspond to known physics. These checks concern the text, not the authenticity of the file.

E = h·ν = 6.626·10⁻³⁴ × 8.35·10²¹ ≈ 5.5·10⁻¹² J ≈ 34.5 MeVAbove about 11.6 MeV, such photons can knock a neutron out of the nucleus of titanium-48: they therefore affect the nuclei, whereas the letter claims the opposite D71 p.507.

h: A metal has no sharp lines
x: solid titanium: shared electrons → continuous energy bandsThe lines in the table are those of isolated atoms, in a gas or a flame. This is why our quantum memories use isolated ions in a transparent crystal, such as europium in an yttrium oxide.

intense lines → return to the ground state within a few tens of nanosecondsAn atom excited on these lines falls back spontaneously almost at once. Our memories use far more stable states: a coherence of six hours was measured on europium spins in 2015.

“12 states or more” · “from zero to twelve” = 13 values · “10 states, hence 2 atoms (10 + 2)”The text wavers between 12 and 13 values D71 p.507 D71 p.508. And two atoms of ten states offer 100 combinations, not 12: the “10 + 2” split does not correspond to any simple coding.

≈ 200 MeV per fission ≈ 3.2·10⁻¹¹ J, against k·T·ln 2 ≈ 2.9·10⁻²¹ J at 300 KEach ODU GOAA operation would release about ten billion times the minimum energy of a logic operation (Landauer limit, 1961). Our quantum machines aim, on the contrary, for reversible, low-dissipation operations.
The idea in one sentence. The XANMOO was not feasible in 1967, but its theoretical ingredients existed: it was conceivable on paper, several decades ahead of the available means.

No one knew how to isolate, see or target a single atom: the first single ion was trapped and observed in 1980, the first single neutral atom in an optical tweezer in 2001. Laser cooling, needed to immobilise the atoms, did not exist before 1978. The laser had existed since 1960, but it could be neither finely tuned onto a line nor moved with atomic precision. The gamma beams of the letter cannot be produced, focused or steered in this way, neither in 1967 nor today. The ODU GOAA, which controls the fission of a single atom, has no known equivalent.

the quantum levels of electrons (Bohr, 1913); the titanium line tables (1939); frequency beating, known since the early days of radio; liquid helium (1908) and the dilution refrigerator (1964); cooled computer memories (the cryotron, 1956).

As the letter describes it, the titanium memory remains unachievable (gamma rays, an absorbed beat, a metal with sharp lines, states that erase within a few nanoseconds). But its general principle, several levels per atom, atoms addressed one by one, a pure and cold crystal, has become real in our qudits, our atoms in optical tweezers and our rare-earth memories, with other atoms and other beams.

h: What level of education was needed to write D71?
x: What the text masters: the computing vocabulary of 1967, down to UNCOL, an intermediate-language project known mainly to professionals D71 p.508; the electronics of triodes and transistors, including the correct point that an amplifier does not create energy D71 p.505; the basics of atomic physics and fission; the use of a table of spectral lines. What it does not master: it confuses lines and states, mixes neutral titanium and the Ti⁺ ion, attributes sharp lines to a metal, ignores that photons of 34.5 MeV affect nuclei, credits the atom with the ability to absorb a beat and wavers in the count of states. A specialist in atomic physics would not have made these errors. Estimate. The text calls for the background of an engineer or senior technician of the 1960s, in electronics or computing, with solid notions of general physics and access to a technical library: today, anywhere from a two-year technical diploma (bac + 2) to an engineering degree. This estimate concerns the text as written; it points to no author.

II · Ummo according to the letters › Beings›Chapter 10 of 31Beings · Chapter 10The BAAYIODUU and evolution In 1967, five letters to AAAlicia Araujo set out “the biogenetic bases” of evolution according to Ummo: 86 pairs of krypton atoms, the BAAYIODUU, which would capture information from the environment and steer mutations towards forms that are already possible. This chapter reports what they say, then compares them with models of evolution, including minority ones. The checks state what present-day physics and biology allow us to assert; they do not claim to close the question.

Double helix, four bases, messenger RNA modelled on DNA, transfer RNA, a codon of three “signs” per amino acid, ribosomes. This is the state of the art in 1967: the genetic code had just been fully deciphered (1961–1966).D58-2 p.288 D58-2 p.292 D58-2
Bullets fired at random at the Parthenon would not carve caryatids: random mutations should produce monsters, not improvements.D58-2 p.293 D58-2 p.294 D58-2
86 pairs of krypton atoms at the ends of the DNA, in every cell, vibrating at 0.2 MHz at 35 °C, whose electrons would be synchronised in all living beings of the cosmos.D58-2 p.294 D58-2 p.295 D58-3

One of the atoms of each pair would contain, “since the generation of the WAAM”, all possible forms of life: from 50,000 to 18 million mutations per node, of the order of 10520 branches in total.D58-3 p.297 D58-3 p.302 D58-4 · D58-5

The other atom would capture the state of the environment (through chemistry and through waves, including the 21 cm hydrogen line) and would trigger the appropriate mutation, chosen from the catalogue.D58-4 p.304 D58-5 p.309 D58-3

Everywhere protozoa are identical; the branches diverge according to the planets, then converge towards the same goal: the human body, the OEMII.D58-3 p.302 Two examples carry the argument. A marsh lizard suddenly acquires webbed feet through an internal mutation D58-2 p.293. A crab on the American coasts turns blue like the rocks covered with bluish algae around it: its eyes perceive the colour, the potassium and nitrogen in its cells vary, the oxygen in the cellular water emits gravitational waves 1039 times weaker than radio waves, and the “dynamic” krypton atom records them “like a tape recorder” D58-4 p.305 D58-5 p.308 D58-5 p.309. The letter also claims that natural selection is “simplistic”: if it eliminated the weak, primitive species would not coexist with evolved species D58-3 p.303.

On the left, the current model of biology. On the right, that of D58. Both explain how a crab ends up resembling its rock; they differ on one precise point: does the mutation know what the organism needs? In the current model, information about the environment enters through differential survival (bottom arrow); the mutation itself ignores the environment. In D58, the information enters through the mutation itself.

h: 3 Chance and selection: the Parthenon argument
x: The image of bullets on the Parthenon describes a chance without memory: each shot starts again from zero. Selection, however, is cumulative. A favourable mutation, even a rare one, is kept and multiplied; the next one starts from there. Chance proposes, the environment sorts, and the sorting builds up from generation to generation. This accumulation is what the analogy leaves out. The simulation below follows 300 crabs whose colour ranges from brown (0) to rock blue (0.8). Three worlds run in parallel, with the same mutation size. Chance + selection (current model): random mutations, visible crabs are eaten more often.Directed mutations (D58): each mutation moves towards the colour of the rock, no sorting.Chance alone: random mutations, no sorting. Predation strength Generation 32. Mean colour: chance + selection 0.78 · directed 0.75 · chance alone 0.20. What the simulation shows. Chance alone drifts without direction: the Parthenon argument holds for it. But chance and selection reach the colour of the rock within a few dozen generations, about as fast as directed mutations. Adaptation alone therefore cannot settle between the two models. An experiment is needed that distinguishes a “blind” mutation from an “informed” one. It exists, and it dates from 1943. The simulation is a toy model (a single characteristic, a single cause of mortality), not a measurement; but the cumulative effect it shows has been measured in nature. In Florida beach mice, the pale coat is due to a specific mutation of the Mc1r gene, selected by predation (Hoekstra et al., 2006); in the peppered moth, the dark form declined when soot disappeared from tree trunks.

h: 4 A key experiment: Luria and Delbrück
x: In 1943, Salvador Luria and Max Delbrück asked exactly the question of D58: when bacteria become resistant to a virus, is it contact with the virus that causes the useful mutation, or did the mutation already exist, having appeared at random before contact? The two hypotheses predict different distributions. If the environment causes the mutation, each culture has the same small chance per cell: the numbers of mutants follow a Poisson distribution, variance equal to the mean. If the mutation is random and prior, a mutation occurring early in a culture produces a “jackpot” of thousands of resistant descendants: the variance becomes enormous. Mutation caused by the environment (D58 hypothesis)Random mutation, before contact (Darwinian hypothesis) Induced: mean 10.1, variance 11, variance / mean ratio ≈ 1.1.Random: mean 2.7, variance 38, ratio ≈ 14; biggest jackpot: 44 mutants. Model: each culture starts from one bacterium and reaches 220 cells; the mutation rate is chosen so that both hypotheses have the same theoretical mean, 10 mutants. Under the random hypothesis, the observed mean varies greatly from one run to the next: this is the effect of the jackpots. Cultures with more than 60 mutants are grouped in the last column. The actual result. Luria and Delbrück observed jackpots: the variance far exceeded the mean. The resistance mutations existed before contact; the environment merely sorted. Joshua and Esther Lederberg confirmed this in 1952 by a direct method, replica plating: the resistant colonies are found on the original plate, which was never in contact with the selective agent. Luria and Delbrück received the Nobel Prize in 1969. These two experiments were published before D58, which does not mention them. The letter claims that terrestrial biologists attribute evolution “to external radiation and to selection” D58-2 p.288: this is a simplified version, which ignores the experimental evidence they already had.

The strongest idea in D58 is not the krypton: it is that of a catalogue of all possible forms of life, of which each planet realises only a tiny part (the possible ones in green, the realised ones in red, D58-3 p.300). Current biology knows very similar notions, without a material support. D58 ideaClose current notionEssential difference All possible forms are “written” in advanceGenotype space: the “Library of Mendel” (Dennett, 1995), neutral genotype networks (A. Wagner, 2014). The theoretical morphospace (Raup, 1966, for shells).This space is defined by chemistry and combinatorics; it is stored nowhere. A sequence of 1,000 bases already offers 41000 ≈ 10602 possibilities, more than the 10520 of D58. Not everything is possible; mutations are “channelled”Developmental constraints and biases (evo-devo), Waddington’s epigenetic landscape and canalisation (1957).The constraints come from physics and from the history of organisms, not from a pre-established list. Convergent evolution towards the same formEvolutionary convergence: the camera eye that appeared several times, the streamlined shape of sharks, ichthyosaurs and dolphins. S. Conway Morris (2003) argues for a convergence towards intelligence.Open debate: S. J. Gould (1989) insists on contingency. Lenski’s experiment (since 1988) shows both: some adaptations repeat, others depend on historical chance. Carbon-based life everywhereMajority position in exobiology: silicon chemistry is far less rich than that of carbon.Probable, but not demonstrated: no other biosphere is known. Simple organisms are identical on all planetsUniversality of the genetic code on Earth: all living beings descend from a common ancestor (LUCA).On Earth, this universality is explained by a common origin, not by a cosmic law. Nothing says that another biosphere would have the same code.

Gradual natural selection is not the only model under discussion. Several researchers have proposed evolution by leaps, or guided by an internal logic. Some of these ideas are close to D58. The diagram shows their essential difference: the way form changes over time. Darwin, 1859 · modern synthesis, 1937–1947

Small random variations, sorted by the environment, accumulated slowly.Status: reference framework, solidly established for the mechanisms; its uniform tempo is debated.With D58: this is the model the letter rejects. Eldredge and Gould, 1972

Species remain stable for a long time (stasis), then change quickly, especially when a new species is born in a small isolated population. “Quickly” means within a few thousand to a few tens of thousands of years.Status: stasis is well documented in the fossils; the debate concerns the share of each tempo. The model keeps natural selection as the mechanism.With D58: the “nodes” where the branches burst out resemble the punctuations, but D58 makes them directed mutations. Goldschmidt, 1940

A single large mutation can suddenly create a new form.Status: long rejected, partly rehabilitated: a mutation in a regulatory gene can change a great deal at once (loss of the pelvis in the stickleback through the Pitx1 gene, Shapiro et al., 2004).With D58: the lizard that suddenly acquires webbed feet is a saltation D58-2 p.293. Teilhard de Chardin, The Phenomenon of Man, 1955

A law of “complexity-consciousness” steers evolution towards man, then humanity converges towards a final point, the Omega point.Status: philosophical and theological vision, widely read in the 1960s, rejected as a scientific theory.With D58: striking parallel. The letter makes the branches converge towards the OEMII, then towards a final node X where man continues his encephalisation and his “mutual agglutination” D58-3 p.302. Anne Dambricourt Malassé, since 1987

Palaeoanthropologist at the CNRS and the Muséum. According to her, the base of the embryonic skull (sphenoid, chondrocranium) tilts in stages over the course of the species: this is the “craniofacial contraction”, which accompanies the straightening of the nervous system and bipedalism. The process is continuous, its effects appear in leaps, always in the same direction, under the effect of a developmental dynamic rather than climatic pressure.Status: published (thesis 1987, Comptes Rendus Palevol 2006), supported by a few researchers (J. Chaline in particular); judged highly controversial by the majority of palaeoanthropologists, who see in it a form of orthogenesis and ask for a genetic mechanism.With D58: this is the closest model. D58 claims to explain “how neuroencephalisation takes place progressively” D58-1 p.285 through directed internal mutations; Dambricourt describes a hominisation in directed stages, of embryonic origin. The difference: she looks for the driving force in development (architect genes, self-organisation), D58 in an external factor received by the krypton. Kimura, 1968 · Laland et al., 2015

Most changes in DNA are neutral and become fixed by chance. The “extended synthesis” adds developmental biases, plasticity, epigenetic inheritance and niche construction.Status: neutralism is accepted for molecular evolution; the extended synthesis is debated.With D58: developmental biases join the idea that not everything is possible, without a pre-established catalogue.

The BAAYIODUU can be read in two ways. The letter gives it a “double mission”: it “stores […] coded information on all possible organic beings”, and it “captures information from the environment” D58-3 p.297. It then specifies that in each pair, one atom contains the “dictionary” of possible forms and the other, the “dynamic” atom, captures and triggers the mutations D58-4 p.304. Another reading, which the letters also allow, makes the krypton mainly an antenna: the information would come from outside, which the synchronism of all living beings of the cosmos suggests D58-2 p.295, and the krypton would merely receive it in order to steer the mutations. This reading removes the objection about storage capacity. Both readings are examined below.

h: If the krypton is an antenna
Receiving a signal stronger than the noise
x: 21.106 cm photon: 5.9·10⁻⁶ eV · thermal agitation at 37 °C: kT ≈ 0.027 eV, i.e. 4,500 times moreAny antenna must distinguish the signal from the noise. Each photon of the hydrogen line carries 4,500 times less energy than the thermal agitation of a water molecule in the body. The value 21.106 cm is correct, but it has been public since its discovery in 1951.

h: Being tuned to the right frequency
x: krypton: first absorption lines around 9.9 eV (far ultraviolet) · hydrogen line: 1,420 MHz · quoted vibration: 0.2 MHzAn antenna responds to the frequencies to which it is tuned. The electrons of krypton absorb in the far ultraviolet, at energies a million times higher than the 21 cm line. Nothing in its known structure makes it sensitive to radio waves.

gravitation / electricity ratio for two electrons: G·mₑ² / (e²/4πε₀) ≈ 2.4·10⁻⁴³The letter has the message pass through gravitational waves emitted by the oxygen in water, 1039 times weaker than radio waves D58-5 p.309. This order of magnitude is consistent with the known weakness of gravitation. But it is also what makes reception impossible with current physics: it took 4 km detectors to capture, in 2015, the waves from two black holes.

modifying a chemical bond of DNA: of the order of 1 to 4 eV · a 21 cm photon: 6·10⁻⁶ eVAfter reception, an action is needed: changing a DNA base requires about a million times the energy of a photon of this line. The letter does not describe this step.

if the environment steers the mutation → useful mutations appear after contact, in proportion to the needThe antenna model has the advantage of being testable: it predicts mutations correlated with need. This is precisely what the Luria and Delbrück experiment (section 4) looked for, without finding it, in bacterial resistance. A positive result in other organisms would be a major discovery.

h: If the krypton is also a memory
A noble gas as a medium
x: Kr: complete shells, non-degenerate ground state ¹S₀ → 0 bits; 1st excited state at 9.9 eV, i.e. 371 times kT at 37 °CA noble gas has full electron shells: its ground state is unique, so it cannot encode information. Its first excited states are so high that body heat never populates them (probability e−371), and they would decay within a few nanoseconds. Only the isotope krypton 83 (11.5% of natural krypton) has a nuclear spin (9/2, i.e. 10 states), used today in MRI.

designating one branch among 10⁵²⁰: 520 × log₂ 10 ≈ 1,727 bits · 172 atoms all krypton 83: ≈ 571 bitsEven in the most favourable case, the 172 atoms do not carry enough to number the branches, still less to describe each form. The letter replies that the positions of the electrons “tend towards infinity” D58-5 p.309; quantum mechanics says the opposite: a bound system of finite size has a finite number of usable states at a given energy (Holevo bound for retrievable information).

decoherence in a warm, wet environment: of the order of 10⁻¹³ s (Tegmark, 2000)“Synchronous” electrons in all living beings on all planets would presuppose a shared and preserved quantum state. According to current physics, such coherence is destroyed within a fraction of a picosecond in a cell at 37 °C, and entanglement alone does not transmit information (no-communication theorem). A still unknown physics would therefore be required.

electron g-factor: measured 2.002 319 304 36…; theory and measurement agree to within 10⁻¹²D58-5 describes quantum mechanics as an “entelechy” and spin as a fragile concept that would not explain the Zeeman effect D58-5 p.307. Spin has explained this effect since 1925–1928, and the magnetic moment of the electron is the best-verified prediction in all of physics. A contextual detail. In 1967, krypton was famous: since 1960, the metre had been defined by a line of krypton 86. The number 86 in the letter has no other established link with this isotope.

Measured against 1967 and the biology of 2026, here is where D58 anticipates, where it joins ideas already known, and where it is wrong. The descriptive part is solid. D58 correctly summarises the molecular biology of 1967: double helix, transcription, translation, three-base codon. It also warns, rightly for the time, of the danger of X-rays in pregnant women D58-2 p.293. The criticism of Darwinism targets a simplified version. The Parthenon argument describes chance without cumulative selection. The letter does not discuss the experiments of Luria and Delbrück (1943) and of the Lederbergs (1952), which already showed, for bacteria, that useful mutations precede contact with the environment. It nonetheless joins a real current of thought. The idea of evolution by directed leaps, driven by an internal logic towards man, exists in Teilhard de Chardin and, in a published and debated scientific form, in Anne Dambricourt Malassé. Punctuated equilibria also show that evolution is not always gradual. The proposed mechanism is not compatible with known physics. Read as an antenna, the krypton would have to pick up signals thousands to billions of billions of times weaker than the thermal noise, on frequencies to which it is not sensitive. Read as a memory, it cannot contain 10520 forms. A still unknown physics would be required. The model nevertheless remains testable: mutations correlated with need would be its signature. What remains innovative lies in the questions rather than the answers. D58 raises three questions that biology took up later: can the environment write into the genome? Yes, in specific cases (CRISPR); are all mutations equally probable? No, their rates are modulated; does evolution explore a constrained and convergent space of possibilities? This is a current debate. On each of these points, the biology of 2026 has found mechanisms, but not that of the krypton.

II · Ummo according to the letters › The language›Chapter 26 of 31The language · Chapter 26How words are made The 542 words of the lexicon are not random strings of letters: they follow spelling habits and are built from roots. This chapter brings these out, with one tool to break down any word and another, the UmmoTron, to make new ones. 68.8%vowels, against about 45% in French or Spanish85.1%of words have a doubled letter89.1%of words end in a vowel35root families identified

The idea in one sentence. The words are a transcription, made by the Ummites themselves, of sounds they consider hard to render with our letters: the spelling varies, but the habits are clear. The letters say that they fix “the acoustic image” of their words “in Spanish spelling”, and that most of their sounds can be written in several ways D41-1 p.79 D37-2 p.71. Vowels dominate: A is the most frequent letter (about 20%), followed by O, I, U; E is rare, unlike in French and Spanish. Syllables are almost always open (consonant then vowel); consonant clusters are rare and mostly limited to M or N before another consonant. Doubling mainly concerns vowels (AA, OO, II, UU, EE), sometimes tripled. Since the number of letters varies for the same word, it probably marks a duration or an intonation rather than a meaning. A word has 8.3 letters on average. A20.1O15.3I14.2U10.3E8.9N3.8M3.5B3.2W3.1Y3.1X2.6D2.6G2.5S1.7L1.6R1T0.6C0.4H0.3Z0.3V0.2F0.2K0.2P0.2 Letter frequency (%) across the 542 entries of the lexicon; vowels are in colour. The lexicon was extracted automatically: variants and a few doubtful entries are included, so the figures are orders of magnitude.

Hypotheses drawn from the data. The letters give almost no sentences translated word for word: a grammar cannot be reconstructed, only the way words are formed. 1
Most long words are assemblies of roots that keep their meaning: a new word is obtained by putting them end to end. D69-2 p.4522

h: The main word most often comes last
x: What qualifies comes first, what is designated comes after: UMMO + AELEWE (committee) gives the council of Ummo; UAMII (meal) + XAABII (room) gives the kitchen; OYAGAA (Earth) + WOA (God) gives Jesus, just as UMMO + WOA gives the divine man of Ummo. D541 p.8123

h: One prefix for the child, another for the union
x: UU before GEE (man) or YIE (woman) designates the child; UUGEEYIE joins the two for “the children”. OMGEEYIE, marriage, also combines man and woman. 4

h: Repetition widens or doubles the meaning
x: WAAM is the cosmos, WAAM-WAAM the set of cosmos. In the “bi-language”, repeating a word (UMMO UMMO UMMO) carries a second thread of ideas at the same time as the first. D41-1 p.82 D731 p.8165
AIOOYA O means “exists”, AIOOYA AMIEE “does not exist”. The same pattern gives AA-INNUO-AIOOYA-AMIE: “symmetry does not exist”. D41-15 p.1576
IAS marks the first, IEN the second: BUAWAA IAS is “soul no. 1”, UAXOO IAS “receiver no. 1”, AAXOO IEN “transmitter no. 2”. D33-3 p.54 D33-3 p.557

A name combines a root and a number, followed by the filiation: D9DEII 98 is the son of D9DEII 97, O9OEOEE 95 the son of O9OEOEE 91. The root is passed on, the number distinguishes. D21 p.13 D57-3 p.267See the map of key figures8

The letters transcribe the sounds “by simulating Spanish spelling”, and the same sound can be written in several ways: X and S alternate (XANMOO and SANMOO, “XI or SI”), doubled vowels vary (BUUAWA, BUAWA, BUAUA), the French translation adds OUs (OUMMO). D37-2 p.71 D41-1 p.79 D32 p.389

The voiceless consonants (P, T, K, F) are almost absent, in favour of N, M, B, W, Y, X, D and G. The letters say that the Ummite vocal organ produces only a restricted range of frequencies; the connection is a hypothesis. D33-3 p.59

Try it. The UmmoTron draws at random roots whose translation is given in the letters (XAABI, house; UAMII, meal; WAAM, cosmos…), assembles them as the compound words of the file do, then translates the resulting word. A nod. The name salutes JPJean-Pierre Petit’s Logotron. In the late 1970s, on one of the first Apple IIs to reach France, he had written a small program that automatically produced neologisms, about 90,000 of them, very few of which existed in French. He even presented it, as a hoax, as a serious linguistic tool on the programme Temps X. The idea became a comic book in 1990, Le Logotron, in Les Nouvelles Aventures d’Anselme Lanturlu (Présence publishers). The program is described on Lanturluland, the site devoted to his comic books, and the word “Logotron” appears in the keyword index of his site jp-petit.org. Difference from the original: the UmmoTron only assembles roots whose meaning is given in the letters, so every invented word has a translation. UIWIBOZOO« the point of the instant »UIW+IBOZOOReversed rootsIBOZOOUIW“the instant of the point”Word composed by the UmmoTron: it does not appear in the letters, but each of its roots does.UIWinstantunit of time, about 3.092 minutes: the time taken by the mass of the C isotope of thorium to halveAttested D21 p.8 D23 p.15 D32 p.39IBOZOOpointpoint, element of the cosmosAttested in (spatial point) D58-5 p.308 ; (I.U) D357-2 p.730 How it works. In the letters, the main root often comes last and those that qualify it come before: UAMII (meal) + XAABII (house) gives UAMIIXAABII, “the house of meals”, that is, the dining room. The UmmoTron applies this rule and translates from right to left. With two roots, it also shows the reversed word: changing the order changes the meaning, like “the house of meals” and “the meal of the house”. Its 77 roots come from the families above and from the short words of the lexicon whose meaning is given. The compound word does not exist in the file, unless the UmmoTron happens to land on a real word: it then points this out. Limit: the order is not always the same in the letters (OOLGA WAAM means “science of the cosmos” there); each translation is one possible reading, not the only one. h: WOA is not the God of the theologians
x: Letter D792 starts from cosmology. The WAAM-WAAM, the multiple universe, receives its information from two poles. From one of them, WOA, “All the possible configurations of matter, all the possibilities of BEING” take their origin Letter 1988 D792-1 p.861. Not every imaginable form is possible, however: a man one millimetre tall or an insect several dozen metres long could not exist, because real beings must obey the physical and biological laws of the WAAM-WAAM Letter 1988 D792-1 p.861. Without this pole, the cosmos would be a “gigantic crystal” with no form and no information Letter 1988 D792-1 p.861. The letter grants that WOA can be compared with God, but at once draws the difference. The God of Earth’s religions is an anthropomorphic being, good, the father of his creatures, revealed to prophets; the idea of WOA, by contrast, is said to have been “induced by scientific means, not theological ones” Letter 1988 D792-1 p.862. The authors say they see in WOA neither a father nor an object of faith: “Only reason and scientific proof allow us to build the body of our doctrine” Letter 1988 D792-1 p.862. Neither UUMMOWOA nor Jesus is said to have wanted to found a Church; the difference lies in their times, one born into a society that does not allow myths, the other into a world of metaphorical language and magical ideas Letter 1988 D792-1 p.862. WOA, pure information, needs a support: it acts on the WAAM B.B., the universe that holds the collective consciousness, through an effect the letter compares to the resonance of two violin strings Letter 1988 D792-1 p.862. It describes it as “gigantic archives” in which an exotic plant and the structure of a laser would be coded alike Letter 1988 D792-1 p.862. The verb “create” does not fit: WOA “has nothing to do with that mythical being created by the minds of earthly man” Letter 1988 D792-1 p.863, and it passes on models rather than drawing matter out of nothing Letter 1988 D792-1 p.864. The letter says it respects its readers’ beliefs and invites them to stay faithful to them, and to read its reports “as one studies the customs of an exotic and distant tribal village” Letter 1988 D792-1 p.864.

h: Nervous networks that change in leaps
x: Under the heading “THE CRITICAL CONFIGURATION OF THE BRAIN”, the letter sums up what it had already sent to correspondents in Canada Letter 1988 D792-1 p.864. It takes up its science of networks: nodes linked by channels of force, energy or information, from the telephone to the car engine, up to human society and the brain, “the most perfect of known networks” Letter 1988 D792-1 p.864 D792-1 p.865. The chapter The network society develops this idea. The key notion is EIDOAYUEE, which the letter translates as “Emergence”: a well-structured network has properties that none of its elements has Letter 1988 D792-1 p.865. A pentagon is in none of its five segments; no single part of a radio set can transmit on its own Letter 1988 D792-1 p.865. The network must also follow a functional model, the GUIXOOEXOO, or the result is a complicated machine that serves no purpose Letter 1988 D792-1 p.866. Above all, emergence moves “in leaps”, in steps: an internal combustion engine can be improved as much as one likes, it will never become a camera Letter 1988 D792-1 p.866. Animal evolution illustrates these steps Letter 1988 D792-1 p.866 D792-1 p.867. In coelenterates, sensitive cells trigger a reflex. In echinoderms, ganglia store memories and the animal adjusts its behaviour to its experience. From fish to mammals, the brain makes decisions, but deterministic ones. Then comes the leap to the human brain, which requires an information density of 1019 bits per cubic centimetre, but above all a new architecture: its emergence is “CONSCIOUSNESS” Letter 1988 D792-1 p.867. This brain connects with the soul (BUAWAA) and the B.B., gains a share of freedom, and becomes a sensor of the multicosmos: what a human being thinks and does, on any cold star, alters the configuration of the WAAM-WAAM, according to the letter Letter 1988 D792-1 p.867.

x: The letter then announces a last leap, “the most transcendent of all”, the OIXIOOWOA function Letter 1988 D792-1 p.868. It first describes how the brain can still evolve. By the natural route, mutations guided by the B.B. change the proteins that build the brain’s architecture Letter 1988 D792-1 p.868 D792-1 p.869; each lineage would have about 218,000 possible mutation models, decoded by a krypton network Letter 1988 D792-1 p.869. A second route, biotechnology, would make it possible to synthesise a more complex genome, with serious ethical stakes Letter 1988 D792-1 p.871. The descendants of Earth people will be more intelligent and freer, but their emergence will stay the same: to observe the universe and pass it on to the B.B. Letter 1988 D792-1 p.869. Yet the more conscious a brain is, the more its action on the multicosmos grows, and not in a linear way: doubling its complexity could multiply its action by six Letter 1988 D792-1 p.870. A “macro brain” of eighty cubic decimetres could in theory dominate the WAAM-WAAM and rival the B.B. Letter 1988 D792-1 p.869 D792-1 p.870. The multicosmos, an organism that corrects itself, prevents this: it would erase such an organism from its universe by a “boundary effect” and turn it into a network of energy in another universe, with no loss of information Letter 1988 D792-1 p.870. For an ordinary person, the letter judges this event impossible in practice, and sees it as a protection: “We can die […] but not ‘disappear by passing into another Cosmos’” Letter 1988 D792-1 p.870. This is where the letter brings back the UAA, the models of conduct. Physical laws, the EEWAO, apply to everything; the UAA, by contrast, address only conscious brains, which remain free to follow them Letter 1988 D792-1 p.871 D792-1 p.873. Without freedom, the multicosmos would be frozen; without UAA, societies would fall into chaos Letter 1988 D792-1 p.872 D792-1 p.873. Like the molecules of a gas, whose pressure can be predicted though the path of each cannot, thinking beings as a whole would end up following them, even if some violate them Letter 1988 D792-1 p.874.

h: The OEMMIIWOA, fourth stage of the brain
x: The letter then distinguishes four stages: the reflex, deterministic processing of information, the conscious human brain, and a fourth, the OIXIOOWOA Letter 1988 D792-1 p.874 D792-1 p.875. The third stage would last between 1.4 and 38 million years; 82% of the civilisations known to the authors, Earth among them, would be in it Letter 1988 D792-1 p.875. A humanity that does not destroy itself ends up passing to the fourth stage Letter 1988 D792-1 p.875. A first mutant almost certainly appears within the first ten million years, then the mutation does not recur for millions of years Letter 1988 D792-1 p.875. This mutant, the OEMMIIWOA, has the same body as a human, but a distinct genome: it is “a new biological species” Letter 1988 D792-1 p.875 D792-1 p.876. Besides the krypton atoms that link every brain to the soul and the B.B., a new krypton network would link it directly to WOA Letter 1988 D792-1 p.876. It thus receives the UAA without going through the B.B., and spreads them into the cultural heritage of its society Letter 1988 D792-1 p.876. The letter credits it with great humility, service to others and flawless conduct; what it thinks of itself depends on its culture, and in a magical culture it may believe itself a God Letter 1988 D792-1 p.877 D792-1 p.882. It can be a woman: that Jesus and UUMMOWOA were men would be “a mere chance circumstance” Letter 1988 D792-1 p.877. Its end is not a death. The letter explains this by the LEIYOO WAAM, the boundary effect: its mass becomes photons in a neighbouring universe and its psyche joins the B.B. directly Letter 1988 D792-1 p.879 D792-1 p.880. It is not a punishment, the letter stresses, but “a law of survival of the Multicosmos” Letter 1988 D792-1 p.880. Jesus and UUMMOWOA would be two examples of OEMMIIWOA Letter 1988 D792-1 p.881. Millions of years after the first, thousands of mutations occur; the new species replaces the old one, then disappears in its turn: this is the “natural death” of a humanity, which affects fewer than 0.002% of cold stars Letter 1988 D792-1 p.881 D792-1 p.882. h: 1 Man, a node in a network
x: The idea in one sentence. For the authors, everything is a network, on three nested levels: the neurons of the brain, the whole body (the OEMII), and society, in which each person is a node. The letter puts it as an insistence: “We have repeated several times that the OEMII is a network, and we consider this concept so transcendental that we prefer to repeat it” Letter 1966 D47-1 p.202. The first level is the brain. Mental life, “being a function of the neuronal network of the encephalon, and this network in turn being linked to the general NETWORK of the OEMII”, cannot be acted on in one part without affecting the whole Letter 1966 D47-1 p.203. The letter rejects two Earth positions at once: the “animist” conception, for which memory would be the work of the soul alone, and that of the “materialist psychologists” who reduce thought to the cortex Letter 1966 D47-1 p.203. The last level is society. Man sees himself there “as a node joined to other nodes by multiple arcs or connections” Letter 1966 D47-2 p.208 D47-2 p.209. The human body “develops in its environment by integrating itself into another much more complex Network (the social Network)” Letter 1966 D41-7 p.123. To give an idea of the complexity of the first level, the letter describes a laboratory screen, at EWO IAAU IU, which represents the brain in 405 sections spread over as many rooms, covering roughly “516,600 square metres” Letter 1966 D47-1 p.204. That is a little over 70 football pitches. The social network. Each person is a node, joined to the others “by multiple arcs or connections”.Figure 1 · Three nested networks. Animated diagram, after D47 and D41-7. The camera dives from the social network into the person, then into the brain: each level is a network, and damage at one level affects the others Letter 1966 D41-7 p.123.

The idea in one sentence. Earth’s doctrines do not fail because they are false, but because the language that should convey them is too poor, and the same for everyone. “YOU USE A STANDARDISED LANGUAGE. The same oral forms for everyone, as if the receiving minds were all identical.” Letter 1966 D47-1 p.201 The link of communication, “LANGUAGE”, is said to be “frighteningly poor”: it faithfully conveys neither emotions nor ideas Letter 1966 D47-1 p.201. People can then be seen arguing for hours only to realise that they are defending “the same concept masked by inadequate words” Letter 1966 D47-1 p.201. The letter extends the observation to wars: by really listening to the adversary, one would often discover “a total incomprehension of motivations” Letter 1966 D47-1 p.201. It reviews Marxism, existentialism, economic liberalism, Protestantism and the Catholic Church. Each camp would know poorly the doctrine it despises, and would ignore “the marvellous fraction of truth that all of them contain” Letter 1966 D47-1 p.201 D47-1 p.202. A common bond would escape them: “HOPE IN A MORE JUST FUTURE EARTH HUMANITY” Letter 1966 D47-1 p.202. “It is not because Earth doctrines are mistaken that they have failed. It is the impossibility of finding means of INFORMATION that are accessible to all humans […]” Letter 1966 D47-1 p.202 The letter does not offer a quick solution. It considers it “utopian” for such a language to be born from a meeting at UNESCO: years of analysis and adaptation would be needed Letter 1966 D47-1 p.202. In the meantime it gives three practical pieces of advice Letter 1966 D47-1 p.202: listen to the other person’s arguments and look for their motivations; never mock their ideas; invite others to formulate “their rigorous criticisms against you”. This advice echoes that of group reading, already presented in Education, section 8.

h: 3 Why man is unhappy: a disorganised network
x: The idea in one sentence. Human unhappiness would come neither from a bad nature nor from the environment alone, but from a network in which the connections between people work badly, and in which defects are passed down from one generation to the next. The question is put without detour: “what is the reason why man is unhappy on EARTH?” Letter 1966 D47-1 p.206. The old adage “man is a wolf to man” is dismissed as a simplistic explanation Letter 1966 D47-1 p.206.

A gold clock, taken apart and put out of order by generations of children, ends up in a pool of mud. A “certain Mr Rousseau” passes by and concludes: “The clock is good; it is the dirty water and the mud that stop it from working”. A companion replies that it has a construction defect and that the clockmaker is responsible Letter 1966 D47-2 p.208. For the letter, both are wrong to reason in terms of “good and bad men”: the factors are multiple Letter 1966 D47-2 p.208.

HeredityMan inherits from his parents nervous reflexes (the instincts), memories that surface in dreams, and “a whole network of nervous connections or conditional synapses” Letter 1966 D47-2 p.208. The networkHe is born a node of a network whose arcs “function in a disastrous manner”: “It is the communication system that is at fault” Letter 1966 D47-2 p.209. DefenceSurrounded by billions of fellow beings, he feels “terribly alone, misunderstood” (the letter speaks of men in the plural), and defends himself against others, “upsetting the network even more” Letter 1966 D47-2 p.209. The loop closes: the brains of the ancestors were vitiated by “this same disorganisation of the social network” Letter 1966 D47-2 p.209. Letter D47-4 describes the same circle for the Ummo of former times: the “aggressive reflexes” born of social tension “ARE TRANSMITTED BY HEREDITY TO ITS CHILDREN” Letter 1966 D47-4 p.221. The “cut wire” of the radio set, which is enough to make the whole network mute, comes from the same letter Letter 1966 D47-2 p.210. It is presented in the chapter Education, section 4, and in the interactive figure of the Encyclopaedia. Organised network.
