x: The idea in one sentence. For the letters, belief in the marvellous owes less to facts than to the need to be admired and a taste for mystery Letter 1967 D62-4 p.371 D62-4 p.372 Letter 1967 D62-7 p.388. They say they were disconcerted on arriving: in the face of a few scientists, superstition and myth “divide and fragment” terrestrial society. Letter 1967 D62-4 p.368The teller of prodigies often repeats what a neighbour saw, swears he saw it himself and ends up believing it. Letter 1967 D62-7 p.388Caught out, he cannot confess without losing face; he flies into a rage, threatens, and his proofs are always mislaid or lent out. Letter 1967 D62-7 p.389An argument from probability: among a million events, one is bound to take a curious form, and someone will see a sign in it. Letter 1967 D62-4 p.372“You label as magic everything you do not know”, as your ancestors did lightning or an eclipse. Letter 1967 D62-4 p.372“It is more beautiful to create a poetic lie than to carry out cold calculations with a computer.” And they quote the Gospel: “only the truth will make you free”. Letter 1967 D62-4 p.372 D62-4 p.373In 1988, another letter speaks of a “collective psychosis” around UFOs, in which “well above 80%” of observations are errors or fakes. Letter 1988 D1378 p.927

ch: Parapsychology: the letters unmask the frauds
x: The comparison with thinkers and institutions of Earth is made by the author of the site; it sheds light on the ideas of the letters, and says nothing about their origin. The letters’ investigations, set among those of the mediums, scientists and sceptics of Earth. On UmmoNeither credulous nor dogmatic: active doubt Letter 1967 D62-2 p.360 Letter 1967 D62-7 p.393David Hume, 1748An Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding, “Of Miracles”: the wise man proportions his belief to the evidence.Marcello Truzzi, 1978; Carl Sagan, 1980“An extraordinary claim requires extraordinary proof.” Truzzi also criticises the “pseudo-sceptics” who deny without examination.Richard Feynman, 1974“The first principle is that you must not fool yourself, and you are the easiest person to fool.”Analysis. The letters’ method is the one that scientific scepticism would formulate in the following years: rule out ordinary causes, demand converging evidence, deny nothing in advance. Their double rejection of credulity and of “fanatical scepticism” closely resembles Truzzi’s distinction. They also apply it to themselves: the same series advises not to believe on trust typewritten sheets coming from elsewhere.On UmmoUnmasking the mediums Letter 1967 D62-3 p.365 D62-3 p.366Harry Houdini, 1924A Magician Among the Spirits; he unmasks the medium Margery before a committee of Scientific American.Edmund Fournier d’Albe, 1921He shows that the “psychic structures” of Kathleen Goligher, studied by Crawford, are muslin.Harry Price, 1931He identifies Helen Duncan’s “ectoplasm” as cheesecloth that had been swallowed and regurgitated.Analysis. The letters’ investigators proceed like Houdini: a conjuror’s eye, a false identity, a witness who pretends to be convinced. Their only advantage is technical, the infrared cameras. But by 1967 ectoplasm was already widely discredited, which the letters acknowledge by citing the American parapsychologists.On UmmoThe Indian rope Letter 1967 D62-4 p.369 D62-4 p.375John Wilkie, Chicago Tribune, 1890Under the name “Fred S. Ellmore”, he publishes an invented account; the retraction, four months later, goes unnoticed.The Magic Circle, 1934It offers a large reward for the complete trick performed in the open air; it is never won.Peter Lamont and Richard Wiseman, Nature, 1996Of some fifty testimonies, the most spectacular are recounted decades after the events.Analysis. For historians, the great rope trick is a legend born of a press hoax; the letters have it actually performed in 1957. They claim never to have “read a single explanation”. Yet the idea of a rigid stick disguised as a rope had been circulating since the early twentieth century: the magician John Nevil Maskelyne reported in 1912 the testimony of an articulated bamboo sheathed in rope. Their version adds the underground accomplice.On UmmoFire walking Letter 1967 D62-7 p.390Johann Gottlob Leidenfrost, 1756A drop on a very hot plate floats on a cushion of vapour.Bernard Leikind and William McCarthy, 1985Embers conduct heat poorly, and the foot touches them only for an instant.Analysis. The letters’ conclusion matches that of the physicists: nothing supernatural. The bouncing drops are the Leidenfrost effect; the letter calls it “skin effect”, the name of an unrelated electrical phenomenon. Current explanations insist less on sweat than on the poor conduction of the embers.On UmmoFolk wisdom confirmed Letter 1967 D62-7 p.392Alexander Fleming, 1928Penicillin, discovered by chance on a contaminated culture dish.Cod-liver oilIts virtues against rickets, explained by vitamin D in the 1920s.The kuroyakiA Japanese folk medicine of charred materials in a sealed vessel.Analysis. The argument is classic and partly right: traditional remedies have received an explanation. The link between mouldy bread and Fleming is looser than the letter says: his discovery was fortuitous. The letters’ KHUROYAKI corresponds to the Japanese kuroyaki.On UmmoRhine and the Nautilus Letter 1967 D62-2 p.362Joseph B. Rhine, Duke University, 1934Extra-Sensory Perception: Zener cards and statistics applied to telepathy.The Nautilus, 1960The French press reports telepathy trials aboard the submarine; Louis Pauwels and Jacques Bergier popularise them. The US Navy denies it.C. E. M. Hansel, 1966ESP: A Scientific Evaluation: Rhine’s results do not withstand strict controls.Analysis. The 1967 letters take the Nautilus experiments for granted, “which you now know from the press”. They are today considered a press rumour. Their confidence in Rhine is consistent with their doctrine, since for them telepathy is an ordinary faculty.

ch: Parapsychology: the letters unmask the frauds
x: A sceptic’s discourse. On mediums, fakirs and healers, the letters speak like a rationalist investigator, close to Houdini or Sagan, with a marked taste for the exposed trick. A constant reserve. They always leave a door open: a case of healing, a telekinesis that is “not impossible”, “authentic” phenomena under study. None is described. The same pattern as elsewhere. The proofs are images and probes that only they possess. The reader can judge the logic of the account, not the facts.

Letter 1967 D62-7 p.392The psychophonies: a deception “in every case” according to a 1987 call, a physical phenomenon in which the recorder becomes a receiver according to another. II · Ummo according to the letters › Society›Chapter 14 of 31Society · Chapter 14Couple and sexuality From 1966 to 1987, several letters describe sexual and conjugal life on Ummo: an upbringing without taboos but extreme modesty, a marriage preceded by an opinion from the computers, fertility regulated without contraceptives, then positions on abortion and on the condition of the women of Earth. The chapter reports these texts, places them in their period and points out their contradictions. The letters also describe intimate practices in detail. A brief ceremony before twelve witnesses, a minister who registers the union, and a marriage that becomes legal only once consummated Letter 1966 D41-13 p.147 Letter 1972 D102 p.611 D102 p.612. He consults the network, which gives a probabilistic opinion; a couple may go ahead regardless, at their own risk. The rare cases of homosexuality are “controlled” by hormonal means; adolescents who show a tendency towards it are educated in mixed groups. The comparison with thinkers and institutions of Earth is made by the author of the site; it sheds light on the ideas of the letters, and says nothing about their origin. On UmmoExplaining sexuality to children Letter 1966 D41-11 p.138Sigmund Freud, 1907“Sexual explanations given to children”: against the stork fable, which ruins the child’s trust.Sweden, 1955First country to make sex education compulsory in schools.France, 1973The Fontanet circular introduces sex education in schools.Analysis. In 1966, in Francoist Spain, these letters hold a very modern discourse: truth, images, absence of shame. They take up Freud’s argument about the stork almost word for word. But they combine it with a very strict bodily modesty and a religious reading of reproduction, which brings them closer to a progressive Catholicism than to the coming sexual revolution.On UmmoA couple chosen with the help of a computer Letter 1966 D41-13 p.146 Letter 1972 D102 p.609Plato, The Republic, Book VThe magistrates arrange the unions of the guardians for the good of the city.Operation Match, Harvard, 1965One of the first computer dating services, based on questionnaires.Analysis. The idea of matching couples by calculation was in the air in 1965. The letters push it far, but keep the decision with the young people, where Plato entrusted it to the State. Their argument remains debatable: an almost zero failure rate also stems from the fact that failure is defined as pathological.On UmmoFertility regulated without contraceptives Letter 1966 D41-12 p.143 Letter 1966 D41-13 p.148Kyusaku Ogino and Hermann Knaus, 1924-1930The rhythm method, based on the date of ovulation.The pill, 1960Authorised in the United States in 1960, in France in 1967 (Neuwirth law), in Spain in 1978.Paul VI, Humanae Vitae, 1968Rejects artificial contraception and admits natural regulation of births.Analysis. The 1966 letter believes that the Church “is beginning to admit” birth control. Two years later, Humanae Vitae adopts exactly their line: no to artificial means, yes to knowledge of the cycle. The Ummite technique is the rhythm method made perfect. By telephone in 1987, however, they judge that birth control “is not an evil” and criticise the theologians.On UmmoA seriousness that grows with development Letter 1987 D539 p.801 D539 p.803Aristotle, then Thomas AquinasThe human soul would come only after several weeks: the thesis of “delayed animation”.Supreme Court of the United States, Roe v. Wade, 1973Protection of the embryo that increases by trimester.Spain, 1985; France, Veil law, 1975Decriminalisation laws, limited in Spain to three cases.Analysis. Their gradation matches both modern law and, paradoxically, the scholasticism they criticise: Thomas Aquinas also thought that the embryo was not immediately animated by a human soul. The letter reaches Spain two years after the 1985 law, in the middle of the debate. Their final position, that the mother decides but frivolity is a fault, is that of a large part of the supporters of decriminalisation.On UmmoMale domination Letter 1987 D540 p.805 D540 p.807 D540 p.809Simone de Beauvoir, 1949The Second Sex: “One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman.”Thomas Aquinas, Summa TheologicaWoman is called there a “misbegotten male”: the letter’s quotation is exact.William Masters and Virginia Johnson, 1966Their studies demolish the Freudian opposition between “clitoral” and “vaginal” women.Analysis. The 1987 letter takes up the themes of the feminism of the 1970s and 1980s: the prehistory of domination, the misogyny of the Church Fathers, the critique of Freud, the “veiled” machismo of the sharing of tasks. Several quotations are exact, others belong to legend, such as the council that supposedly debated whether women have a soul. Above all, it contradicts the 1966 letter, which described women as submissive at home and “more masochistic”.On UmmoHomosexuality as a tendency to be corrected Letter 1966 D41-12 p.143 Letter 1966 D41-13 p.146Spain, 1954 and 1970Homosexuals are targeted by the Vagrancy Act, then by the Social Danger Act, until 1979.American Psychiatric Association, 1973Homosexuality is removed from the list of mental disorders.World Health Organization, 1990In turn removes it from its classification of diseases.Analysis. In 1966, treating homosexuality with hormones is a common medical idea; the letters present it with benevolence, in a country that punished it. Since then, medicine has abandoned this approach, and several countries, including France in 2022, ban practices aimed at changing sexual orientation.

A mirror of the 1960s. The 1966 letters combine the progressive ideas of their time (upbringing without taboos, marriage for love, family planning) with its medical and moral norms: modesty, the husband’s authority, homosexuality as something to be treated. A dated evolution. The 1987 letter on women and the one on abortion closely follow the Spanish debates of the Transition. The portrait of the Ummite woman changes between the two, without the difference being explained. A model they refuse to export. Each time, the letters warn that their customs must not serve as a model for Earth.

The site warns that its documents “may be apocryphal”. Analysis of the sound reveals a 50 Hz mains hum and a brief voice, syllable by syllable, which transcription software cannot match to any known language. The cleaned version removes this hum; it is the site’s own processing. The recording is reproduced here as an item of the file, without attribution. Listen: one sentence, two voicesEarthling voice (in French)0:000:05Ummite voice (reconstruction, in French)0:000:05“Nous ne venons pas de votre planète, mais nous vous ressemblons beaucoup” (“We do not come from your planet, but we look very much like you”). This is not a recording but a reconstruction: a synthetic voice brought down to a single note, made nasal, stripped of its bass and harmonics, and evened out syllable by syllable. It follows the witnesses, who describe a voice that is “soft”, “monotonous, without inflection”, “nasal”, and the letter on the laryngeal transducer: “the bass and the harmonics are not emitted”. External document 1967 E38 p.1146 External document 1984 E17 p.1003 Letter 1966 D33-3 p.59 How the sound was analysed Spectrogram. The sound, cut into slices of a few milliseconds, is broken down into frequencies (Fourier transform). It is cut off sharply at 12 kHz and its two channels differ slightly: signs of an analogue copy. Hum. Constant peaks at 99, 148, 248 and 297 Hz, multiples of 49.5 Hz: the signature of European mains current at 50 Hz, on a tape that runs about 1% too slowly. Cleaning. Notch filters remove 49.5 Hz and its multiples, and a filter suppresses the low end of the spectrum below 120 Hz: the hum drops by 20 to 27 dB, while the voice band does not move. Sounds. In the telephone band (300 to 3,400 Hz), 59 brief sounds with a median of 0.16 s, at 1.6 per second, against 4 to 6 syllables per second in normal speech. Voice. The pYIN algorithm measures a pitch varying between 120 and 200 Hz, around 160 Hz; harmonic sounds (spectral flatness of 0.002), with a vowel resonance around 700 Hz: a human voice. Transcription. The Whisper large-v3 model recognises no language (32% at best, against more than 90% for clear speech) and detects no Spanish speech. A software failure does not prove the absence of words: a human ear may hear what it misses. The file’s calls. JLJosé Luis Jordán Peña’s thrombosis, in green, falls between the last direct calls and the letters dictated by an intermediary.

ch: Behind the scenes of the file
x: A familiar pattern. Anonymous documents, devoted intermediaries, objects that cannot be examined, a late and contested confession: the affair combines features found in the great hoaxes of the twentieth century. A singularity. Few hoaxes have, as here, announced in advance their own possible falsity: “Do not believe us” makes every denial compatible with the story. An open question. Peña’s confession is the strongest item against an Ummite origin, but its contradictions prevent it from being treated as proof; the compilation classifies it among the external documents, without deciding.

ch: The Ummites as Seen by Earthlings

ch: The Ummites as Seen by Earthlings
h: 6 Meals, sleep, bath: the night of 26 May 1967
x: The idea in one sentence. External document 1967 E3 p.962She refuses the bed and sleeps on the floor in the dining room, on a layer of foam that the secretary sprays onto the ground; in the morning, “even with a magnifying glass nothing was left”. External document 1967 E3 p.962 E3 p.963They use the bath, but neither the towels nor the soap. ch: The Ummites as Seen by Earthlings

ch: The Ummites as Seen by Earthlings
x: The idea in one sentence. The typist describes a meticulous, almost obsessive writing workshop, which he understands as a school of discipline External document 1969 E8 p.976. ch: The Ummites as Seen by Earthlings
x: The idea in one sentence. This is the field where the witnesses feel most sure of themselves, and where they give the least proof: the objects appear one evening, work, then leave with their owners External document 1966 E31 p.1057 External document 1967 E7 p.973. The images follow the descriptions and dimensions given by the witnesses; the rest is interpretation.

ch: The Ummites as Seen by Earthlings
x: Artist’s impression. The three sizes described: a walnut, a steel sphere with three holes, a tennis ball.This is the object that tipped the typist over. A sphere “the size of a walnut” floats in his flat, stops at different heights, leaves the room, comes back “as if directed by radio” and hides in the bookshelf. A handwritten note gives it a name and a measurement: UULUEWA, 2.19 cm in diameter External document 1966 E31 p.1057 E31 p.1058. The Ummites explain to him that it contains “a kind of microphone”: this is how they heard his quarrels with his wife. In another letter, he describes a small sphere “like steel, with 3 holes”, motionless in the air External document 1966 E31 p.1058 External document 1967 E30 p.1053. On the evening of 26 May 1967, a leather suitcase contains about twenty of them, the size of a tennis ball or smaller. The visitors place them one by one on the balcony “like bubbles”, and they disappear into the street; four remain in the corridor External document 1967 E3 p.961. What the letters say. A letter describes the UULUUEWAA: small spheres with detectors, which fly like insects and whose presence is said to have made the typist nervous; they carry a gravity sensor in a boron crystal. See Technologies. Letter 1987 D2655 p.946

ch: The Ummites as Seen by Earthlings
x: Artist’s impression. The “ulodooisagii” box and its opalescent screen, after the professor of medicine.The most precise account comes from the professor of medicine who doubts Ummo. In early January 1966, he receives a box measuring 8 × 8 × 5.3 cm, made of a metal he cannot identify. On top, a square opalescent screen; the metal “seemed to merge with this translucent plate without any break”. Underneath, five holes, one of them square External document 1967 E9 p.981. Guided by telephone, he sees in it a living synapse, in which one can make out “the molecular structure of acetylcholine”, in colour and in three dimensions. The device is named to him “ulodooisagii”. A stranger takes it back after 48 hours External document 1967 E9 p.982. According to EVVillagrasa, he is said to have filmed it in 8 mm Kodacolor External document 1967 E38 p.1147. Artist’s impression. The screen where the typist sees himself move; the “three-dimensional” photographs.The evening D9DEI 98 comes to convince him, he takes out a device: on a small flat screen, the image of the typist’s office, “as if in relief and of an extraordinary colour”. He sees himself move on it “as on a miniature cinema screen” External document 1966 E31 p.1057. The photographs have the same effect. They are shown, then taken back. At FSSesma’s, his wife and son see them for a few minutes before the messenger leaves again with them; he had first been promised a “meteorite-monitoring device”. A neighbouring photographer asserts that relief cannot be seen without an optical device. They show a part of the human body “in all colours and in relief” External document 2005 E55 p.1262 External document 1966 E1 p.954 External document 1967 E30 p.1053. What the letters say. Letters of 1967 describe a camera with no glass lens and no negative, producing a stereoscopic colour image, and a lens made of heated gas. See UULAYA NAI and UULAXAA in Technologies. Letter 1967 D65 p.401 D65 p.405 D65 p.409

ch: The Ummites as Seen by Earthlings
h: THE INSTRUMENTS OF THE NIGHT OF 26 MAY
x: Artist’s impression. The humming “fountain pen” and the rod of the silent visitor.Before the superior’s arrival, the couple turn off the light and open the balcony. One of the visitors stays motionless, eyes closed. The other takes out “a sort of fountain pen” that emits “a continuous humming with highs and lows”: the typist understands that “something was being communicated to them” External document 1967 E3 p.960. Later, the silent one handles “a metal rod with a disc in the middle”, which the typist draws in his letter. No one tells him what it is for External document 1967 E3 p.961. Artist’s impression. The foam bed and the superior’s night light.At bedtime, the secretary asks permission to “put something on the floor”. She takes out a nickel-looking cylinder “which emitted an incredible quantity of foam” and left a large stain, “as if it had been varnished”. The superior settles on it. In the morning, the yellow stain has gone External document 1967 E3 p.962 E3 p.963. For light, a disc “a little larger than a fifty-peseta coin”, very phosphorescent, placed on the floor, lets the typist’s wife see her in the dark External document 1967 E3 p.963.

ch: The Ummites as Seen by Earthlings
x: Artist’s impression. The “radioactive” pellets of the Segovia bridge.One Saturday afternoon in 1967, the typist acts as cover: he pretends to take photographs while D3DAA 3 places, near the Segovia bridge in Madrid, small pieces “the size of a fingernail”, taken from a very thick metal box and painted pink or mother-of-pearl. He buries some, slips others against the pillars of the balustrade; his companion throws two balls into the Manzanares. They are, he says, “radioactive markers” for measurements External document 1967 E7 p.972 E7 p.973. After the June departure, the typist returns with a screwdriver, extracts one without touching it and throws it into the river. Fifty years later, Peter Heubi describes a brown pellet “looking like varnished paint” stuck to the collar of his jacket, impossible to peel off, then vanished by itself External document 1967 E7 p.973 External document 2017 E47 p.1241. Artist’s impression. The ring that applies the seal, the pellet-staple at the top of the bundle; the stamp is that of the letters.The seal is applied in front of the typist with “a sort of ring worn on the finger”, pressed on an ink pad. The sheets are joined by “a small metal pellet” that serves as a staple, then the bundle is photographed External document 1968 E29 p.1049. The ink varies by country: orange and coarse on documents posted from Australia, “dark, yellowish” in Mexico, dark on the letters received in London External document 1970 E23 p.1024 E23 p.1028 External document 2017 E47 p.1242.

ch: The Ummites as Seen by Earthlings
x: Artist’s impression, after the dimensions published in 1967. A pencil gives the scale.These are the only objects that Earthlings have kept. After 1 June 1967, a metalworker, a resident of Santa Mónica, then children pick up small silvery tubes. A circular letter offers a reward for recovering them and gives their dimensions: 129.8 mm long, 8.3 mm calibre, a central disc of 24 mm; “a polished aluminium cylinder with its ends rounded in the shape of an ogive” External document 1967 E10 p.986. The second typist obtains one from a mason’s son, for a tip; inside, “a blade made of a material that resembles plastic”. Two capsules end up in Paris, with a commission that judges their technology superior to known techniques External document 1967 E19 p.1014 External document 1968 E13 p.993. What the letters say. The letters also speak of capsules left at Aluche in 1966; their fate and that of the tubes are summarised in Behind the Scenes of the File. Letter 1966 D38 p.73

ch: The Ummites as Seen by Earthlings
x: Artist’s impression. The stone with twenty signs, broken in three, and the professor’s crystals.The first object in the Spanish file is a red stone, announced to FSSesma by telephone in January 1966. Artificial and rounded, it bears twenty signs said to sum up “the quintessence of a civilisation more than 300,000 years old”. It broke into three External document 2005 E55 p.1262. The professor of medicine hands the typist rectangular crystals for the Ummites, “with coloured spots in the centre”. The text does not say what they contained External document 1966 E1 p.953. Gap. The typist himself asks the question: if they want to be believed, “let them show the device I saw working”. He says he holds “one of their devices”, without ever producing it. In 2005, Peña would say he had used a model hanging from a nylon thread for the photos of the craft. External document 1966 E31 p.1057 External document 1967 E7 p.973 External document 2005 E41 p.1210

ch: The Ummites as Seen by Earthlings
x: The idea in one sentence. A single account of a cure, reported by the family, who themselves do not believe in an extraterrestrial origin External document 1984 E17 p.1003 E17 p.1005. ch: The Ummites as Seen by Earthlings
The Ummites as Seen by Earthlings
x: Nordic type, monotone throat voice, sobriety, strict hierarchy, extreme politeness, erudition, taste for secrecy, flying spheres, three-dimensional photos.

ch: The Ummites as Seen by Earthlings
h: What rests on a single witness
x: The night of 1967, the three-dimensional screen, the foam cylinder, the pellets of the Segovia bridge, the typing with the knuckles, the earlobe-less ear.

ch: The Ummites as Seen by Earthlings
x: No object shown except the tubes; anonymous witnesses; hotels, registration numbers and “one of their devices” announced but never produced External document 1967 E7 p.973. Seen by Earthlings, the Ummite is neither a monster nor an angel: he is a foreigner who is too well brought up, too learned and too discreet. His only stable physical sign is the voice. II · Ummo according to the letters › Knowledge›Chapter 20 of 31Knowledge · Chapter 20Space, time and logic The Cosmology chapter shows in animations what the letters claim about the cosmos. This one follows their reasoning: how they reduce space to a field, dimension to an angle, and movement to an illusion, and why they say we must step outside two-valued logic. Sources: mainly the 1966 and 1967 letters to Fernando FSSesma and Enrique EVVillagrasa (D52, D59-1 to D59-3), then two letters from 1987 (D357-2, D731) and a letter from 2004 (NR-20). The coloured figures come from the letters; the two diagrams without a page frame are our own. 1966space “is identical” to the force field D52 p.2393IOAWOO angles make up our three dimensions D59-2 p.327≈ 20universes known to the Ummites according to D357-2 D357-2 p.72310⁴bits per cm³ in the collective soul D357-2 p.736

h: 1 Space is only a perceived force field
x: The idea in one sentence. For D52, space and the force field are not two distinct realities: it is the action of the field on our nerves that consciousness translates into “space” Letter 1966 D52 p.239. The letter starts from symmetry. A right shoe and a left shoe have the same shape but cannot be superimposed: they are “INNUO VIAAXOO” bodies, enantiomorphs Letter 1966 D52 p.237. It announces that this notion will later explain why our cosmos is the “ENANTIOMORPH” of the anticosmos Letter 1966 D52 p.239. D52: two enantiomorphic bodies (image 1) and two superimposable pyramids (image 2) D52 p.238D52: a symmetric body and its plane of symmetry (image 3) D52 p.238 Two bodies of the same shape, symmetrical about a plane: they are enantiomorphic.body Aits reflection Bplane of symmetryAnimated diagram. After images 1 to 3 of D52: we try to superimpose a body and its reflection, then two pyramids. It then defines the field as in an Earth textbook: a large sphere attracts a small sphere placed at 144 ENMOO, the more strongly the closer it is Letter 1966 D52 p.237 D52 p.238. Then it raises the questions that this diagram leaves open: what is mass? Are mass and volume one and the same thing Letter 1966 D52 p.238? D52: a small sphere attracted towards the central mass, and the field represented by force vectors D52 p.239 The closer a sphere is to the mass M, the more it is attracted: this is the letter’s field of forces.MABCAnimated diagram. After image 4 of D52: three small spheres fall towards the mass M; the arrows represent the field, the hollowed sheet the space identified with it. The shape of the sheet is an illustration; the letter does not give it. Its answer proceeds in two stages. There is indeed an external reality, but it is as different from perception as “a mountain is from the word M - O - N - T - A - G - N - E” Letter 1966 D52 p.238. And above all: “FORCE FIELD AND SPACE are identical”. The action of the gravitational field on our nerve endings “gives rise in our consciousness to this illusion that we call SPACE” Letter 1966 D52 p.239. The letter nevertheless allows, “for convenience”, continuing to speak of length as a dimension Letter 1966 D52 p.239. The colour and heat produced by a single stimulus, mentioned on the same page, are presented in Cosmology, section 1.

h: 2 A dimension is an angle, not a length
x: The idea in one sentence. Where Earth physics measures lengths on axes, the letters retain only angles between elements; three of these angles are enough to make up our three dimensions Letter 1967 D59-2 p.318 D59-2 p.327. D59-2 first describes the most refined Earth conception it knows of: phase space, where the “point” is a small volume of at least h³, since the uncertainty principle forbids locating a particle at a precise point Letter 1967 D59-2 p.317. It immediately departs from it: “Our conception of UXGIGIAM (SPACE) is radically different” Letter 1967 D59-2 p.317. The disagreement concerns the word dimension. On Earth, it evokes a straight line, a “SCALAR” quantity. For the authors, dimensions are associated “with ANGULAR QUANTITIES”; Earth’s physicists, they add, “do not attribute a dimensional character to the angle” Letter 1967 D59-2 p.318. Each IBOZOO UU is a bundle of three axes that never intersect. Neither has a position: only the angle IOAWOO exists, between a direction of one (violet) and a direction of the other (turquoise).IBOZOO UU (Ψ)IBOZOO UU (Γ)Θ = 23°Animated diagram. After D59-2 (images 10 and 11): two IBOZOO UU rotate freely; the angle Θ between one direction of each, copied at the bottom, varies continuously. The letters warn that these “axes” are a teaching image. The mathematical version replaces the axis with a hyperplane of order 4, taken in a neighbouring IBOZOO UU. Three angles, denoted Ψ, Ξ and Ω, called IOAWOO, “will each define the respective values of three-dimensional space as we conceive it”. An infinitesimal variation of these angles corresponds to “a linked pair of IBOZOO UU” Letter 1967 D59-2 p.327. D59-2: the IOAWOO angle between the OAWOO of two IBOZOO UU (image 11) D59-2 p.321 The IBOZOO UU and the IOAWOO angle are animated in Cosmology, section 6.

h: 3 A lone IBOZOO UU is an empty set
x: The idea in one sentence. An IBOZOO UU only makes sense in relation to another; taken alone, the letter calls it “empty”, and it justifies its existence by the coherence of the model, not by a detection Letter 1967 D59-2 p.321. The reference frame can never be taken within the IBOZOO UU itself: it “MUST BE PROVIDED BY ANOTHER IBOZOO UU”. The letter draws a postulate from this, given in its own language: “IIAS IBOZOO UU AIOOYEDOO (THERE EXISTS IN ABSOLUTE TERMS NO ISOLATED IBOZOO UU)” Letter 1967 D59-2 p.321. It confronts this with set theory: if the IBOZOO UU belongs to the WAAM, the element taken in isolation is written “I = ∅ (An IBOZOO UU considered as a set is empty)”. It sees in this a “glaring contradiction” with the classical propositions of that theory Letter 1967 D59-2 p.321. Then comes the objection: how can we know that the IBOZOO UU exists, if nobody has detected it? The word “detection”, the letter replies, is “inappropriate”: the model built on this hypothesis “has so far satisfied all the explanations” of the behaviour of matter and energy Letter 1967 D59-2 p.321. The letter returns to this further on with an Ummite word: an isolated IBOZOO UU is AIOOIEDOO, a “false, absurd concept” Letter 1967 D59-2 p.330.

h: 4 How the brain makes a straight line
x: The idea in one sentence. What we see as a straight line would be our brain’s sorting of IBOZOO UU arranged by their angle, like dragonflies arranged by shade of green Letter 1967 D59-2 p.327 D59-2 p.328 D59-2 p.329. The image of the “swarm of dragonflies”, mentioned in Cosmology, has a sequel Letter 1967 D59-2 p.327 D59-2 p.328: the dragonflies are of every colour, and no two have exactly the same tone; an exceptional eye picks out all the green ones and arranges them by shade, from light green to the darkest; “this is where the brain makes us form a wrong judgement”: instead of a range of greens, we would see “a cold, abstract straight line”; the light green pair becomes the near end, the blue-green pair the far point. A swarm of dragonflies of every colour: no two have the same shade.light green: nearblue-green: farAnimated diagram. After D59-2 (images 19 and 21): the swarm, then the sorting of the greens by shade, perceived as a receding straight line. Without the image, the letter says the same thing: the neurencephalon sorts the IBOZOO UU “into an ordered scale according to their angular magnitude relative to one of them taken as a reference”. This sorting becomes the mental image of “DISTANCE” when no matter lies between the eye and the object Letter 1967 D59-2 p.329. D59-2: the brain sorts the IBOZOO UU according to their angle (image 19) D59-2 p.329 Two warnings follow. The IBOZOO UU are not small spheres, and saying that “between them there is a void” makes no sense. Yet this is the image formed by a child on Ummo when told about space for the first time: he imagines the WAAM as “an immense spawn of UYAAAYAA”, an arthropod that drags a pouch of transparent eggs Letter 1967 D59-2 p.329. D59-3 clarifies one word: a “straight line” of IBOZOO UU is not a geodesic, since arcs of different apparent lengths may correspond to the same chain. The authors prefer to call it a “GEOID” Letter 1967 D59-3 p.332.

The idea in one sentence. A particle does not move: one IBOZOO UU stops “presenting” it while its neighbour presents it in turn Letter 1967 D59-2 p.328. The string of firecrackers in D59-4 is animated in Cosmology, section 7. The two preceding letters give two other images.

We must abandon the idea of a particle passing from a point P to a neighbouring point P′. In a pair of linked IBOZOO UU, the first “by inverting its axes, ceases to present itself as a particle”, while the second orients itself to become an identical particle. Two conjurors stand ten metres apart: one puts a marked rabbit into his pocket, the other takes one out a moment later. “Any intelligent person will easily understand that the rabbit did not travel through the air and that there are two identical rabbits” Letter 1967 D59-2 p.328.

Is an orange held in the hand the same one a microsecond later? The physicist would say that its electrons have changed place but remained the same. For the letter, “this is an error”: another IBOZOO UU now represents the electron Letter 1967 D59-3 p.336. A panel of light bulbs draws a capital A; at the next instant, the A has moved, but it is other lamps that are lit. The next one lights up before the previous one has gone out Letter 1967 D59-3 p.336 D59-3 p.337. D59-3: the A that “flows” across the mosaic of bulbs (image 28) D59-3 p.337D59-3: the electron passes from one lamp to the next (image 29) D59-3 p.338 The “A” seems to slide to the right. No bulb moves: others light up, and the next one lights up before the previous one goes out. For D59-3, this is how an electron “moves”.Animated diagram. h: 6 A time with no point-like instant and no simultaneity
x: The idea in one sentence. The instant can never be reduced to a point, and two distant places have no common “now” Letter 1967 D59-3 p.333 D59-3 p.338. Lived time is first of all a perception: even with our eyes closed, we feel it passing thanks to the body’s rhythms, from circulation to fat metabolism. For the physicist, it is a dimension, at least for the followers of Einstein’s relativity Letter 1967 D59-3 p.332. The letter rejects this idea without adopting its opposite: “It is not that time is quantised; it is that, among other things, an instant cannot be conceived as a point on the time axis”. The interval dt can tend towards zero, but never be as small as we wish Letter 1967 D59-3 p.332 D59-3 p.333. It calls this elementary interval UIWIIOO, the instant Letter 1967 D59-3 p.336. D59-3: the OAWOO that generates time (image 26) D59-3 p.336D59-3: two instants, T₁ and T₂ (image 27) D59-3 p.336 It then represents the “I, now” by a plane, in a WAAM taken as the set of IBOZOO UU “past, present and future” Letter 1967 D59-3 p.337. The “I” of this diagram is not a person but a single particle, a proton for example Letter 1967 D59-3 p.338. For a distant point, the time axis is oriented differently: “One cannot therefore say, for example, that “NOW” such-and-such a thing happens on the planet VENUS, because such a concept of simultaneity has no meaning” Letter 1967 D59-3 p.338. D59-3: the “I now” plane, the past and the future (image 30) D59-3 p.338 Each IBOZOO UU carries its own time axis (arrow). The golden plane is “me, now”: perpendicular to my axis. Far away, the axis is oriented differently: its “now” (pink) does not coincide with mine. No simultaneity.ME (a proton)distant point (“Venus”)Animated diagram. After images 26, 27 and 30 of D59-3: a chain of IBOZOO UU, each with its own time axis, and the “I now” plane. The progressive tilt of the axes is an illustration. A note compares this model with Einstein’s, “not so different”: it would suffice to replace the “SPACE-TIME CONTINUUM” with a “discrete set […] of IBOZOO UU”. Einstein would merely have overlooked that the speed of light is constant only in one frame among others. The note promises to explain later the contradictions between quantum mechanics and relativity Letter 1967 D59-3 p.338. Time as an enrichment of information and the family of limit speeds are presented in Cosmology, sections 9 and 10.

h: 7 Two identical IBOZOO UU are one
x: The idea in one sentence. If two distinct elements take the same orientation, they must be said to be the same, which requires stepping outside two-valued logic Letter 1967 D59-3 p.333. Let us imagine an infinity of small balls, each of a different colour and shade. If two of exactly the same colour are found, ordinary logic will say that they are two, since they are in two places Letter 1967 D59-3 p.333. For the IBOZOO UU, the letter demands the opposite: when two of them, hitherto distinct by the orientation of their axes, become equal, one must “use another reasoning dissociated from divalent logic” and state that these “two” IBOZOO UU are the “same”. A neutron and a pion, which in one frame seem to belong to two different galaxies, may have to be considered as one in another frame Letter 1967 D59-3 p.333. The same page draws a limiting consequence. In the frame where the speed of light would be infinite, all the IBOZOO UU would be identified with a single one, which “has no PHYSICAL reality”: the WAAM would there be “non-existent”, WAAM AIOOIEDOO Letter 1967 D59-3 p.333. The letters’ four-valued logic is presented in Mathematics.

The idea in one sentence. There would be as many pairs of cosmos as there are speeds of light; the Ummites are said to know about twenty of them, and suspect that they are infinite in number Letter 1987 D357-2 p.723. Four types of mass. In each pair of cosmos, there are +m, −m, and two “imaginary” masses, (+√−1)m and (−√−1)m. “Non-real” does not mean “non-existent”, but “situated in another frame”. Letter 1987 D357-2 p.723As many pairs as there are speeds of light. “It is clear that there can exist as many pairs of cosmos as there are speeds of the electromagnetic quanton.” This is the link between the family C₀ … Cₙ of D59-3 and the pluricosmos. Letter 1987 D357-2 p.723 Letter 1967 D59-3 p.333No Anti-Earth. The twin anticosmos is not a copy of our own: “there is no twin anti-UMMO or Anti-Earth”. Letter 1987 D357-2 p.723About twenty known universes. Some by detection, others by journeys, two by deduction. The author writes: “I myself have travelled through another WAAM”. Letter 1987 D357-2 p.723Two inaccessible universes. No ship can go there. One, with neither mass nor anticosmos, is a static network of IBOZOO UU that “EXISTS and DOES NOT EXIST”: it houses the souls. Letter 1987 D357-2 p.723 The universe of souls and that of the collective soul are presented in Spirituality; the pluricosmos in Cosmology, section 11.

h: 9 Measuring the collective soul: a calculation that holds up
x: The idea in one sentence. D357-2 gives the information density of the collective soul (the B.B.) twice, in two different units; once converted, the two values agree Letter 1987 D357-2 p.736. The letter first gives “8.345.10⁷¹” bits per cubic WAALI, the WAALI being worth about 43,700 light-years. It adds that the B.B. would reach no more than 10⁴ bits per cm³, against 10¹⁹ for a human brain Letter 1987 D357-2 p.736. Calculation step (our own)Value 1 light-year9.46 × 10¹⁷ cm1 WAALI = 43,700 light-years4.13 × 10²² cm 1 cubic WAALI7.07 × 10⁶⁷ cm³8.345 × 10⁷¹ bits ÷ 7.07 × 10⁶⁷ cm³≈ 1.2 × 10⁴ bits per cm³ The result falls back on the 10⁴ bits per cm³ announced. The letter also compares this density with that of “this typewritten sheet” Letter 1987 D357-2 p.736: a typed page of about 3,000 characters, on a sheet of 6 cm³, gives a few thousand bits per cm³, the same order of magnitude. These calculations check the internal consistency of the figures, not their reality. They hold only with the WAALI of this letter: a 1966 letter gives 124.3 light-years (see Mathematics).

h: 10 AÏOOYAOU: the shadow before the wave
x: The idea in one sentence. Letter NR-20 names AÏOOYAOU the state of a phenomenon known only by its effects, sometimes even before it occurs Late letter 2004 NR-20 p.1398. It starts from the forecast nebulae, presented in Cosmology, section 4. The drop in temperature “apparently precedes the distortion itself”, without causing it. The proposed image: a shadow cast in our WAAM by the wave that clouds of imaginary matter cause in the anti-universe OUWAAM Late letter 2004 NR-20 p.1398. The model is used to programme the computer of each ship. It gives the amplitude of the fold, but not its moment: “We sometimes have to wait several months before an expedition, prepared in a few days, begins its journey” Late letter 2004 NR-20 p.1398. AÏOOYAOU more generally designates “the state of an indeterminate phenomenon whose emergence is perceptible or highly predictable but of which several actualisations are conceivable”. It tips towards true or false when the phenomenon arrives, or when one is sure that it will not arrive Late letter 2004 NR-20 p.1398. The same page introduces “retropositivity”: an act judged negative at the time, whose consequences, assessed before performing it, would largely compensate for the harm done. The authors call it “crucial” in medicine and education Late letter 2004 NR-20 p.1398. The letter ends with a warning: its claims are “unverifiable sentences of dubious origin, no doubt written by a joker” Late letter 2004 NR-20 p.1398.

h: 11 What current physics allows us to say
x: The idea in one sentence. Each idea has an Earth equivalent that can be named; none is confirmed, and several cannot be tested today. What the letter saysWhat comparable existsWhat cannot be verified Space is only the field D52 p.239In general relativity (1915), gravitation is the geometry of space-time; the idea of a space made of relations goes back to Leibniz.That space is an “illusion” produced in the brain is a philosophical thesis, not a measurement. Dimension is an angle D59-2 p.318In the International System, the angle is a “dimensionless” quantity (the radian); metrologists have proposed making it a base quantity.A space made only of angular relations has no known testable formulation. An element exists only in relation to another D59-2 p.321Relational approaches to physics (Mach; relational interpretation of quantum mechanics, 1990s).These are interpretations; they predict no new measurable effect. A space and a time without point or instant D59-3 p.333Planck length and time; loop quantum gravity and causal sets, which assume a granular space-time.No experiment has yet shown any graininess of space-time. No simultaneity between distant places D59-3 p.338Special relativity (1905): simultaneity depends on the observer. The letter itself cites Einstein.This is established for relativity; the explanation through the orientation of the IBOZOO UU is not. A particle that does not travel; two identical ones are a single one D59-2 p.328 D59-3 p.333In quantum field theory, a particle is an excitation of a field, and two electrons are rigorously indistinguishable. Wheeler suggested in 1940 that all electrons might be just one.Wheeler’s idea has not become an accepted theory. The speed of light changes from one frame to another D59-3 p.333Variable speed of light theories, proposed from the 1990s onwards.None is confirmed; measurements show no variation. Imaginary masses faster than light D357-2 p.723The tachyon, a hypothetical particle of imaginary mass, named by Feinberg in 1967.No tachyon has been observed. About twenty known universes D357-2 p.723Multiverses of several theories (Everett interpretation, 1957; eternal inflation, 1980s).No other universe is observable by our means. An information density of the universe D357-2 p.736Bekenstein bound (1981) on the information contained in a region of space.The letter’s value cannot be measured. The table compares without concluding: it says neither that the letters anticipated Earth science, nor that they copied it.

Promised reports. D52 announces explanations of the ten-dimensional WAAM, of the asymmetry that makes our cosmos enantiomorphic to the anticosmos, and of the polarisation of particles for travel. D59-3 promises to explain the contradictions between quantum mechanics and relativity. These follow-ups are not identified in the compilation. Letter 1966 D52 p.239 Letter 1967 D59-3 p.338A doubtful value. D52 leaves the wavelength of red blank, filled in by hand with “398 mµ”, a value that corresponds rather to violet. Letter 1966 D52 p.239Two WAALI. The calculation in section 9 only holds with the 43,700 light-years of D357-2; another letter gives 124.3 light-years. Letter 1987 D357-2 p.736A warning from the letter itself. D59-2 considers it preferable for Earth to discover these truths slowly, for as long as it takes spiritual values to prevail over “the aggressive instincts of certain economic oligarchies”. Letter 1967 D59-2 p.328 The chapter reports the letters’ reasoning on space and time, without judging their accuracy or the authenticity of the file. The idea in one sentence. The Ummites count in dozens rather than tens, and their units of length and time are defined from physical phenomena.

Ummite mathematics uses base 12, for “purely historical” reasons, even though the Ummites, like us, have ten fingers. D21 p.6An attached table matches our mathematical symbols with theirs (figure below). D21 p.7Another letter judges this difference in symbols to be “superficial”: a simple conversion from base 12 to base 10 is enough. D59-2 p.315 The table of symbols, touch to enlarge. D21 p.7

In base 10, each place is worth ten times the previous one: units, tens, hundreds. In base 12, each place is worth twelve times the previous one: units, dozens, then 144 and 1,728. Two more digits than ours are therefore needed, for ten and eleven. Here they are written A and B; their real symbols are in the table above.

The idea in one sentence. For the Ummites, anything made of interconnected elements (a circuit, pipes, a society) is described with the same mathematical tool: the network.

A network (AYUBAA) is a set of nodes, each endowed with a potential, linked by directed arcs that carry a flow. Examples given: the circuit of a television set, and the pipes of a city, where the potential is the water pressure and the flow is its rate. D31 p.36The theory that studies them, the AYUBAAEWAA, is presented as the equivalent of our set theory, extended to interconnected sets; our network and set theories would be only parts of it. D31 p.36A society is a network, the AYUYISAA: people are the nodes, and the arcs are relationships of consanguinity, mental subordination, or verbal or telepathic communication. Potential and flow are replaced there by psychometric and sociometric parameters. D31 p.36Hence the letter’s diagnosis: the malaise of Earth society would come from the structure of its communications, and not from the brains taken one by one. D31 p.36 D31 p.37The word AYUYISAA also designates, elsewhere, the Ummite State. D68-1 p.422

The idea in one sentence. Our logic knows only true and false; to speak of physical space, the letters say that four are needed.

The principle of the excluded middle (every proposition is true or false) does not hold for the study of space. The Ummites use a four-valued mathematical logic there, the UUWUUA IES. D59-2 p.316They keep two-valued logic for everyday life and for macrophysical phenomena. D59-2 p.316The word AIOOYA translates our verb “to exist, to be”, with nuances of its own. D41-15 p.157 Three statements serve as a starting point: AIOOYA OEMII, man exists; AIOOYA AMMIE WOA, God exists; AIOOYA AMMIE BUUAWA, the soul exists. D33-1 p.41

The four names and their translations come from a single letter. D59-2 p.316 It gives no example for each value. Discrepancy: what does AIOOYA AMMIE mean? The letter on logic translates it as “true outside the WAAM” D59-2 p.316. Another translates AIOOYA AMMIE WOA as “God exists” D33-1 p.41. A third explains that AIOOYA AMIIE would be translated word for word as “does not exist”, and is used for WOA and for abstract ideas, because they have no dimensions D79 p.540. The three perhaps converge (what exists outside our universe), but the letters do not put it that way.

The idea in one sentence. An isolated electron behaves randomly; according to the letters, it is this freedom that allows the soul to act on the body, through a few krypton atoms in the brain.

The universe has two levels: the microphysical, governed by indeterminacy, and the macrophysical, subject to statistical laws and therefore deterministic. D33-1 p.44The letters take up Heisenberg’s uncertainty principle: for an electron in an atom, to speak of determinism makes no sense; it is chance. D33-2 p.46Yet a single quantum of energy, or a single electron, can be enough to command the whole body. D33-2 p.45Isolated krypton atoms have been found in the brain, always in the same place. D33-3 p.47 Their electrons did not move at random but according to a periodic law, and this movement preceded the person’s voluntary gestures. D33-3 p.50

Example What the tool shows. The orange dot is the nucleus. In “ordinary” mode, each blue dot is a possible position of the electron, drawn at random: together, they form a cloud. In “krypton” mode, the position follows a regular law and traces a clean curve. The gauge on the right gives the energy level.To do. Choose a mode. “Absorb” raises the electron by one level (a grain of light arrives), “Emit” lowers it again (a grain of light leaves). Energy level: bas. Ordinary electron: no position is predictable, only the cloud is.Origin of the figures. The drawing is an image by the site. Two points come from the letters: changing level does not mean moving away from the nucleus but changing state, hence a cloud that keeps its size D33-3 p.48; this change is a quantum leap, IBOAAYANUUIO D33-3 p.49. Discrepancy: the krypton lead. The letter puts this lead at 0.0000000755 UIW and adds “around a millionth of a second”. D33-3 p.50 With 3.092 minutes per UIW, that comes to about 14 millionths of a second (calculation by the site).

Two kinds of pulses leave the brain, like the picture and synchronisation of a television signal: some carry the message (0.0001385 s each), the others, longer (0.006385 s), designate the recipient. D33-3 p.60 Another letter gives 0.00013851 s for the message pulse. D45 p.198The transmitters are two krypton atoms, the receiver a third. D33-3 p.51To designate the recipient, the letter uses the image of a million safes with six-digit combinations: only the one whose combination matches opens. The brain, for its part, uses a sequence of about 1,700 binary digits. D33-3 p.60
